nahhas-meani:36-36.t:
His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَٱعْبُدُواْ ٱللَّهَ وَلاَ تُشْرِكُواْ بِهِ شَيْئاً﴾.
That is: do not worship anything else alongside Him, so that your worship becomes void.
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿وَبِٱلْوَالِدَيْنِ إِحْسَاناً﴾.
That is: He enjoined you with this; the implied form is: «and do good to the parents, a doing of good (إحساناً)».
His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَٱلْجَارِ ذِي ٱلْقُرْبَىٰ﴾.
He is the one between whom and you there is kinship.
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿وَٱلْجَارِ ٱلْجُنُبِ﴾.
Ibn ʿAbbās said: he is the stranger, and so it is in the language; from it comes «so-and-so is a أَجْنَبِيّ (a stranger)», and likewise الجَنَابَة: remoteness.
The lexicographers recited:
فَلاَ تَحْرِمَنِّي نائِلاً عن جَنَابَةٍ * فإنِّي امْرُوٌ وَسْطَ القِبَابِ غَرِيْبُ
(Do not deny me a gift because of remoteness, for I am a man who is a stranger amid the tents.)
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿وَٱلصَّاحِبِ بِالْجَنْبِ﴾.
It is narrated from ʿAlī, ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd and Ibn Abī Laylā that they said: الصاحب بالجنب (the companion at one's side) is the wife.
Mujāhid, ʿIkrima, Qatāda and al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: الصاحب بالجنب is the companion on a journey.
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿وَٱبْنِ ٱلسَّبِيلِ﴾.
Qatāda, Mujāhid and al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: he is the guest.
السبيل in the language is the road; he is attributed to it because it is to the road that he resorts.
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لاَ يُحِبُّ مَن كَانَ مُخْتَالاً فَخُوراً﴾.
المختال in the language is one possessed of conceit (الخُيَلاء).
If it is asked: why is the conceited person mentioned here, and how does this speech resemble what came first?
The answer is that among people there are those who are haughty towards their relatives when they are poor, so Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made known that He does not love whoever is like that.

nahhas-meani:37-37.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ٱلَّذِينَ يَبْخَلُونَ وَيَأْمُرُونَ ٱلنَّاسَ بِٱلْبُخْلِ وَيَكْتُمُونَ مَآ آتَاهُمُ ٱللَّهُ مِن فَضْلِهِ وَأَعْتَدْنَا لِلْكَافِرِينَ عَذَاباً مُّهِيناً﴾.
Ibrāhīm, Mujāhid and Qatāda said: this was revealed concerning the Jews.
It is a good view according to the linguists, because the Jews were miserly in telling of the description of the Prophet ﷺ, which they had in the Torah, and they concealed what Allah had given them of His bounty, that is, what He had granted them.
The proof of this is His saying: ﴿وَأَعْتَدْنَا لِلْكَافِرِينَ عَذَاباً مُّهِيناً﴾.

nahhas-meani:38-38.t:
Then He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿وَٱلَّذِينَ يُنْفِقُونَ أَمْوَالَهُمْ رِئَـآءَ ٱلنَّاسِ﴾.
Ibrāhīm said: by it He also means the Jews.
Someone else said: by it He means the hypocrites.
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿وَلاَ يُؤْمِنُونَ بِٱللَّهِ وَلاَ بِٱلْيَوْمِ ٱلآخِرِ وَمَن يَكُنِ ٱلشَّيْطَانُ لَهُ قَرِيناً فَسَآءَ قِرِيناً﴾.
That is: whoever accepts what Satan makes attractive to him — evil as a deed is his deed.

nahhas-meani:40-40.t:
His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لاَ يَظْلِمُ مِثْقَالَ ذَرَّةٍ﴾.
That is: the weight of a ذرّة. One says: «this is the مثقال of this», that is, the weight of this.
مِثْقال is on the pattern مِفْعال, from الثُّقْل (heaviness).
الذَّرَّة is the small ant.
ʿAṭāʾ ibn Yasār narrated from Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī that the Prophet ﷺ said: "Whoever has in his heart the weight of a ذرّة (مثقال ذرة) of faith will come out of the Fire." Then Abū Saʿīd said: if you doubt, then recite: ﴿إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لاَ يَظْلِمُ مِثْقَالَ ذَرَّةٍ﴾.
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿وَإِن تَكُ حَسَنَةً يُضَاعِفْهَا وَيُؤْتِ مِن لَّدُنْهُ أَجْراً عَظِيماً﴾.
Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said: He means Paradise.
The meaning of ﴿يُضَاعِفْهَا﴾ is: He makes it manifold.
Abū Rajāʾ al-ʿUṭāridī read: ﴿يُضَعِّفْهَا﴾.
The meaning of ﴿مِنْ لَدُنْهُ﴾ is: from Him.

nahhas-meani:41-41.t:
His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿فَكَيْفَ إِذَا جِئْنَا مِن كُلِّ أُمَّةٍ بِشَهِيدٍ وَجِئْنَا بِكَ عَلَىٰ هَـٰؤُلاۤءِ شَهِيداً﴾.
There is an ellipsis (ḥadhf) in the speech because the hearer knows it; the meaning is: how will their state be when We bring from every nation a witness? And in the speech there is the sense of rebuke.
ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd said: the Prophet ﷺ said to me: "Recite to me." I said: shall I recite to you when it was revealed to you? He said: "Yes." So I recited to him from the beginning of al-Nisāʾ until I reached His saying: ﴿فَكَيْفَ إِذَا جِئْنَا مِن كُلِّ أُمَّةٍ بِشَهِيدٍ وَجِئْنَا بِكَ عَلَىٰ هَـٰؤُلاۤءِ شَهِيداً﴾, and I saw his eyes shedding tears.
And he said: (شَهِيْدَاً عَلَيْهِمْ مَا دُمْتُ فِيهِمْ فَلَمَّا تَوَفَّيْتَنِي كُنْتَ أَنْتَ الرَّقِيْبَ عَلَيْهِمْ). «[Translator's note: the subject of «he said» is not specified in the source; the quoted words are from al-Māʾida 5:117.]»

nahhas-meani:42-42.t:
His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿يَوْمَئِذٍ يَوَدُّ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ وَعَصَوُاْ ٱلرَّسُولَ لَوْ تَسَّوَّىٰ بِهِمُ ٱلأَرْضُ﴾.
Mujāhid and Abū ʿAmr read: ﴿لَوْ تُسَوَّى بِهِمُ الأَرْضُ﴾.
Whoever reads ﴿تَسَّوَّى﴾, its meaning, according to what is narrated from Qatāda, is: if only the earth would be rent open with them so that they sank into it.
And it is said — and this is clearer — that the meaning is that they wished they were dust like the earth, so that they and it would be level; this is indicated by ﴿يَا لَيْتَنِي كُنْتُ تُرَاباً﴾.
Likewise «تُسَوَّى»: if only Allah, Mighty and Majestic, would level them, so that they became dust like it.
The first reading agrees with their saying «كُنْتُ», and they did not say: كُوِّنْتُ (I was made to be).
It is narrated from al-Ḥasan regarding His saying ﴿تُسَوَّىٰ بِهِمُ ٱلأَرْضُ﴾ that he said: it splits open and is levelled over them.
He holds that the meaning of «بهم» is «عليهم», so the «باء» is in the sense of «على», just as «في» is in the sense of «على» in His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He:
﴿وَلأُصَلِّبَنَّكُمْ فِيْ جُذُوْعِ النَّخْلِ﴾.
Then He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿وَلاَ يَكْتُمُونَ ٱللَّهَ حَدِيثاً﴾.
So it is said: have they not said: ﴿وَاللَّهِ رَبِّنَا مَا كُنَّا مُشْرِكِيْنَ﴾?
There are several answers to this.
Among them: that it falls within the wish, so the meaning is: they wish that they would not conceal any statement from Allah; it is then like your saying: «would that I might meet so-and-so and speak to him».
Qatāda said: these are different stations on the Day of Resurrection; this happens in some of them.
Some of the linguists said: they are not able to conceal, because Allah knows what they keep secret.
And it is said: their saying ﴿واللَّهِ رَبِّنَا مَا كُنَّا مُشْرِكِينَ﴾ — in their own view they were truthful in this; on this view ﴿وَلاَ يَكْتُمُونَ ٱللَّهَ حَدِيثاً﴾ is resumptive (mustaʾnaf).

nahhas-meani:43-43.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ لاَ تَقْرَبُواْ ٱلصَّلاَةَ وَأَنْتُمْ سُكَارَىٰ حَتَّىٰ تَعْلَمُواْ مَا تَقُولُونَ﴾.
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: that is, drunk (سكارى) with sleep.
ʿIkrima and Qatāda said: this is abrogated.
Qatāda said: the prohibition of wine abrogated it.
He holds that the meaning of سكارى is drunk from drink.
The proof that this view is the correct one is that ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, may Allah have mercy on him, said: the prayer was called, and the crier of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ proclaimed: "Let no drunk person approach the prayer."
And it is narrated that one of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ led a group in prayer and recited ﴿قُلْ يَا أَيُّهَا الكَافِرُونَ﴾ and confused it, so there was revealed: ﴿لاَ تَقْرَبُواْ ٱلصَّلاَةَ وَأَنْتُمْ سُكَارَىٰ﴾.
Then this was abrogated by the prohibition of wine.
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿وَلاَ جُنُباً إِلاَّ عَابِرِي سَبِيلٍ حَتَّىٰ تَغْتَسِلُواْ﴾.
ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās and Anas said: except that you pass through, and do not sit.
It is narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās: he is the traveller who passes by the mosque, going through it.
It is narrated from ʿĀʾisha, may Allah have mercy on her, that she menstruated while she was in iḥrām, and the Prophet ﷺ said to her: "Do what the pilgrim does, except that you do not circumambulate the House."
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿وَإِنْ كُنْتُمْ مَّرْضَىٰ أَوْ عَلَىٰ سَفَرٍ أَوْ جَآءَ أَحَدٌ مِّنْكُمْ مِّن ٱلْغَآئِطِ﴾.
Some of the jurists said: the meaning is «and one of you comes from the privy» (with «and»).
This is not permissible according to the grammarians of sound reasoning, because «أو» has its meaning and the «و» has its meaning; in their view this is by way of ellipsis.
The meaning is: if you are sick with an illness in which you are unable to touch water, or on a journey and do not find water, and you need water.
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿أَوْ لاَمَسْتُمُ ٱلنِّسَآءَ﴾.
Ibn ʿAbbās said: ﴿لاَمَسْتُمْ﴾ means you had intercourse.
It is also read: ﴿أَوْ لَمَسْتُمْ﴾.
Muḥammad ibn Yazīd «[Translator's note: al-Mubarrad]» said: whoever holds that it is intercourse, it is better for him to say (لَمَسْتُمْ), like «غَشِيتُمْ», since this act is attributed to the man alone; and whoever holds that it is something short of intercourse, it is better for him to say (لاَمَسْتُمْ).
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿فَتَيَمَّمُواْ صَعِيداً طَيِّباً﴾.
The meaning of (تَيَمَّمُوْا) is: aim for and intend. One says: تيمّمتُ such-and-such and تأمّمتُه when you intend it.
الصعيد in the language is the face of the earth, whether there is dust on it or not.
The proof of this is His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَتُصْبِحَ صَعِيدَاً زَلَقَاً﴾.
It is only called صعيد because it is the furthest the earth rises to.
الطيّب is the clean.
* Then He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ كَانَ عَفُوّاً غَفُوراً﴾.
Because He, Majestic and Mighty, has pardoned and made things easy in tayammum.

nahhas-meani:44-44.t:
His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿أَلَمْ تَرَ إِلَى ٱلَّذِينَ أُوتُواْ نَصِيباً مِّنَ ٱلْكِتَابِ﴾.
The exegetes said: He means the Jews by it, because they had the description of the Prophet ﷺ.
The meaning of ﴿يَشْتَرُونَ ٱلضَّلاَلَةَ﴾ is: they cling to it, and they have become like the purchaser of it; the Arabs say of everyone who desires something: he has bought it.
And the meaning of ﴿وَيُرِيدُونَ أَن تَضِلُّواْ ٱلسَّبِيلَ﴾:
that is, they want you to stray from the path of truth.

nahhas-meani:45-45.t:
Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿وَٱللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ بِأَعْدَائِكُمْ﴾.
That is: so He suffices you against them.
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿وَكَفَىٰ بِٱللَّهِ وَلِيّاً وَكَفَىٰ بِٱللَّهِ نَصِيراً﴾.
Abū Isḥāq «[Translator's note: al-Zajjāj]» said: the باء entered into ﴿وَكَفَىٰ بِٱللَّهِ﴾ only because the speech carries the sense of a command; the meaning is: be content with Allah as protector, and be content with Allah as helper.

nahhas-meani:46-46.t:
Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿مِّنَ ٱلَّذِينَ هَادُواْ يُحَرِّفُونَ ٱلْكَلِمَ عَن مَّوَاضِعِهِ﴾.
It is possible that the meaning is: «Have you not seen those who were given a portion of the Book from among those who are Jews». This is the most likely to be correct, because the two statements and the two meanings are a description of one kind of people, namely the Jews, and this is how the exegesis came.
It is possible that the meaning is: «and Allah suffices as helper against those who are Jews».
And it is possible that the meaning, according to the school of Sībawayh, is: «from among those who are Jews there are some who distort words from their places», then the noun was omitted.
The grammarians recited:
لَوْ قُلْتَ مَا فِي قَوْمِهَا لَمْ تِيثَمِ * يَفْضُلُها في حَسَبٍ وَمبْسِمِ
(If you said "there is not among her people anyone who surpasses her in lineage and smile", you would not sin.)
They said: the meaning is: «if you said: there is not among her people anyone who surpasses her»; then أحد was omitted.
The meaning of ﴿يُحَرِّفُوْنَ﴾ is: they alter; from it comes «تحرّفتُ عن فلان», that is, I turned away from him. So the meaning of ﴿يُحَرِّفُوْنَ﴾ is: they turn away from the truth.
His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَيَقُولُونَ سَمِعْنَا وَعَصَيْنَا وَٱسْمَعْ غَيْرَ مُسْمَعٍ﴾.
It is narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās that he said: that is, they say: hear — may you not hear.
Al-Ḥasan said: that is, hear, without anything being heard (غير مُسْمَع) from you, that is, without being accepted from you.
Were it so, it would have been «غير مسموع»!
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَرَاعِنَا﴾.
The Muslims were forbidden to say it, and were commanded to address the Prophet ﷺ with reverence and veneration.
Al-Ḥasan read: ﴿وَرَاعِنَاً﴾ with tanwīn, making it from الرُّعونة (folly).
We have explained it exhaustively in Sūrat al-Baqara.
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿لَيّاً بِأَلْسِنَتِهِمْ وَطَعْناً فِي ٱلدِّينِ﴾.
That is: they twist their tongues and turn away from the truth.
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿وَلَوْ أَنَّهُمْ قَالُواْ سَمِعْنَا وَأَطَعْنَا وَٱسْمَعْ وَٱنْظُرْنَا لَكَانَ خَيْراً لَّهُمْ وَأَقْوَمَ﴾.
The meaning of ﴿انْظُرْنَا﴾ is: wait for us.
The meaning of ﴿سَمِعْنَا﴾ is: we accepted.
﴿لَكَانَ خَيْرَاً لَهُمْ﴾: that is, with Allah, Majestic and Mighty.
﴿وَأَقْوَمَ﴾: that is, and more correct in judgement; and الاستقامة (uprightness) is from it.

nahhas-meani:47-47.t:
Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿وَلَكِنْ لَعَنَهُمْ اللَّهُ بِكُفْرِهِمْ فَلاَ يُؤْمِنُونَ إلاَّ قَلِيْلاً﴾.
It is possible that the meaning is: they do not believe except with a little belief that does not merit the name of faith.
And it is possible that the meaning is: they do not believe, except a few of them.
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَآ ٱلَّذِينَ أُوتُواْ ٱلْكِتَابَ آمِنُواْ بِمَا نَزَّلْنَا مُصَدِّقاً لِّمَا مَعَكُمْ مِّن قَبْلِ أَن نَّطْمِسَ وُجُوهاً فَنَرُدَّهَا عَلَىٰ أَدْبَارِهَآ﴾.
It is narrated from Ubayy ibn Kaʿb that he said: before We lead you astray with a leading astray after which you will not be guided.
He holds that it is a figurative representation, and that if they did not believe this would be done to them as a punishment.
Mujāhid said: it means in error.
Qatāda said: its meaning is: before We make the faces into napes.
The meaning of ﴿مِّن قَبْلِ أَن نَّطْمِسَ وُجُوهاً﴾ according to the linguists is: We remove the noses, the lips, the eyes and the eyebrows; ﴿فَنَرُدَّهَا عَلَىٰ أَدْبَارِهَآ﴾: We make them napes.
If it is asked: why was this not done to them?
There are two answers to this.
One of them: that only their leaders were addressed with this, and they were among those who believed. This view is narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās.
The other view: that they were warned that this would be done to them on the Day of Resurrection.
Muḥammad ibn Jarīr «[Translator's note: al-Ṭabarī]» said: this did not happen because a group of them believed.
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿أَوْ نَلْعَنَهُمْ كَمَا لَعَنَّآ أَصْحَابَ ٱلسَّبْتِ﴾.
Qatāda said: or We transform them into apes and swine.

nahhas-meani:48-48.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لاَ يَغْفِرُ أَن يُشْرَكَ بِهِ﴾.
And He has said: ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ يَغْفِرُ الذُّنُوْبَ جَمِيْعَاً﴾, and this is well known.
The meaning is that it is said: «I forgive you every sin», and that which it is known you do not forgive is not excepted.
It is narrated that the Prophet ﷺ recited: ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ يَغْفِرُ الذُّنُوبَ جَمِيعَاً﴾, and a man said to him: O Messenger of Allah, and shirk? So there was revealed: ﴿إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لاَ يَغْفِرُ أَن يُشْرَكَ بِهِ وَيَغْفِرُ مَا دُونَ ذَلِكَ لِمَن يَشَآءُ﴾.
Some of the linguists said: its meaning is: except the major sins.
And it is said: its meaning is: after repentance.

nahhas-meani:150-150.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ يَكْفُرُونَ بِٱللَّهِ وَرُسُلِهِ وَيُرِيدُونَ أَن يُفَرِّقُواْ بَيْنَ ٱللَّهِ وَرُسُلِهِ وَيقُولُونَ نُؤْمِنُ بِبَعْضٍ وَنَكْفُرُ بِبَعْضٍ﴾.
Qatāda said: They are the Jews and the Christians. The Jews believed in Moses, the Torah and the Gospel, and disbelieved in Jesus and the Gospel; and the Christians believed in Jesus and the Gospel, and disbelieved in Muḥammad and the Qurʾān. [Translator's note: the text says the Jews believed in "the Torah and the Gospel" and then disbelieved in "Jesus and the Gospel"; translated as written.]
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿وَيُرِيدُونَ أَن يَتَّخِذُواْ بَيْنَ ذٰلِكَ سَبِيلاً﴾.
Qatāda said: They adopted Judaism and Christianity and innovated them, and abandoned the religion of Allah, Islam, with which no prophet was ever sent except with it.

nahhas-meani:153-153.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿فَقَدْ سَأَلُواْ مُوسَىٰ أَكْبَرَ مِن ذٰلِكَ فَقَالُوۤاْ أَرِنَا ٱللَّهَ جَهْرَةً﴾.
Qatāda said: That is, openly before their eyes (ʿiyānan).
Abū ʿUbayda said: It is a qualification of the saying, and the meaning is: "They said openly (جَهْرَةً): Show us Allah."
The view held by the people of reasoning is Qatāda's view.
And the meaning is: they said, "Show us Allah in a manifest seeing," because whoever knows Allah has already seen Him in terms of knowledge.

nahhas-meani:154-154.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَرَفَعْنَا فَوْقَهُمُ ٱلطُّورَ بِمِيثَاقِهِمْ﴾.
الطُّوْرُ: the mountain.
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿وَقُلْنَا لَهُمُ ٱدْخُلُواْ ٱلْبَابَ سُجَّداً﴾.
Qatāda said: We used to be told that it is one of the gates of Jerusalem (Bayt al-Maqdis).
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿وَقُلْنَا لَهُمْ لاَ تَعْدُواْ فِي ٱلسَّبْتِ﴾.
Qatāda said: They were forbidden to catch fish on the Sabbath day.
And one says: عَدَا، يَعْدُو، with the maṣdars (verbal nouns) عُدُوَّاً، عُدْوَانَاً، عَدَاءً and عَدْوَاً, when someone oversteps what is right.
And it is read: ﴿تَعَدُّوا﴾, in the sense of "تعتدوا" (transgress).

nahhas-meani:155-155.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿فَبِمَا نَقْضِهِم مِّيثَاقَهُمْ﴾.
(مَا) is redundant (zāʾida) for emphasis; it conveys the meaning of your saying "truly" (ḥaqqan).
And concerning its meaning there are three views:
The first of them: Qatāda said: The meaning is: "So for their breaking of their covenant We cursed them"; so according to Qatāda's view this was omitted because the hearer knows it.
Al-Kisāʾī said: It is attached (mutaʿalliq) to what precedes it. And the meaning is: "So the thunderbolt seized them for their wrongdoing"; then He conjoined to that up to His saying: ﴿فَبِمَا نَقْضِهِم مِّيثَاقَهُمْ﴾.
So he claimed that He explained "their wrongdoing" (ظُلْمهم), on account of which the thunderbolt seized them, by what comes after it: their breaking of their covenant, their killing of the prophets, and the rest of what He set out of their affairs in which they wronged themselves.
And this is an error and a mistake, because those whom the thunderbolt seized were in the time of Moses, while those who killed the prophets and accused Mary with the slander came long ages after Moses, upon him be peace; so those whom the thunderbolt seized were not seized because of their accusing Mary with slander.
And Qatāda's view is the most deserving of them to be correct.
Abū Jaʿfar said: Abū Isḥāq said: The meaning is: "So for their breaking [of their covenant] We forbade them good things that had been made lawful for them"; and their breaking of the covenant is that it had been taken from them that they would make clear the description of the Prophet ﷺ, but they broke that and concealed it.
[Translator's note: the passage announces three views but explicitly presents those of Qatāda, al-Kisāʾī and Abū Isḥāq, without numbering the second and third; translated as written.]
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَقَوْلِهِمْ قُلُوبُنَا غُلْفٌ بَلْ طَبَعَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَيْهَا بِكُفْرِهِمْ﴾.
Qatāda said: ﴿غُلْفٌ﴾, that is, they do not understand.
And the meaning of ﴿بَلْ طَبَعَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَيْهَا﴾ is: He sealed them as a requital for their disbelief.
And it is a figurative representation (tamthīl); one says: طَبَعَ السَّيْفُ يَطْبَعُ طَبَعاً, when rust covers it.

nahhas-meani:157-157.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَمَا قَتَلُوهُ وَمَا صَلَبُوهُ وَلَـٰكِن شُبِّهَ لَهُمْ﴾.
Mujāhid said: They killed a man whom they imagined to be Jesus ﷺ, and Allah raised Jesus up alive.
Qatāda said: Jesus said: "Which of you will have my likeness cast upon him, and be killed, and enter Paradise?" A man among them said: "I," and he was killed.
Someone else said: They will be punished on the basis that they killed a prophet, because that was their intention.
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿وَإِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱخْتَلَفُواْ فِيهِ لَفِي شَكٍّ مِّنْهُ﴾.
Because their statements about him differ, and they are in doubt about him.
* And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَمَا قَتَلُوهُ يَقِيناً﴾.
The meaning according to the lexicographers is: "And they did not slay the knowledge (of it) with certainty."
Just as one says: "I slew it in knowledge," and "I slew it in certainty," when you have known it with complete knowledge.
Abū ʿUbayd said: If the meaning were "And they did not kill Jesus with certainty," He would have said only: "وما قتلوهُ".

nahhas-meani:159-159.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَإِن مِّنْ أَهْلِ ٱلْكِتَابِ إِلاَّ لَيُؤْمِنَنَّ بِهِ قَبْلَ مَوْتِهِ﴾.
Concerning the meaning of this verse there are three views:
The first of them: al-Zuhrī narrated from Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab, from Abū Hurayra, from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: "The son of Mary will surely descend as a just judge; he will surely kill the Antichrist (al-Dajjāl), surely kill the swine, and surely break the cross, and prostration will be one, to Allah, the Lord of the worlds."
Then Abū Hurayra said: Recite, if you wish: ﴿وَإِن مِّنْ أَهْلِ ٱلْكِتَابِ إِلاَّ لَيُؤْمِنَنَّ بِهِ قَبْلَ مَوْتِهِ﴾. Abū Hurayra said:
"Before the death of Jesus," repeating it three times.
And Qatāda said: ﴿قَبْلَ مَوْتِهِ﴾: before the death of Jesus.
(b) And Ibn ʿAbbās said: ﴿قَبْلَ مَوْتِهِ﴾: before the death of the one who is from the People of the Book.
Al-Ḥasan and ʿIkrima held this view.
And this view was narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās by ʿIkrima.
And Saʿīd ibn Jubayr narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās that the meaning of ﴿قَبْلَ مَوْتِهِ﴾ is: before the death of Jesus ﷺ.
(c) Others besides these said: The meaning is: "And there is not one of the People of the Book but will surely believe in Muḥammad ﷺ before his death."
And these views are not contradictory, because the truth becomes clear to him at his death, so he believes at a time when belief does not benefit him.
Muḥammad ibn Jarīr said: The most deserving of these views to be correct and sound is the view of whoever said: its interpretation is "but will surely believe in Jesus before the death of Jesus," and that this concerns a particular group of the People of the Book, the people of one era among them being meant by it, not the people of all the eras that came after Jesus, and that this will be at his descent; and Muḥammad has not been mentioned in the verses before it, such that it would be permissible to refer the hāʾ in ﴿لَيُؤْمِنَنَّ بِهِ﴾ to him as being a mention of him; rather ﴿لَيُؤْمِنَنَّ بِهِ﴾ comes in the context of the mention of Jesus, his mother and the Jews.

nahhas-meani:160-160.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿فَبِظُلْمٍ مِّنَ ٱلَّذِينَ هَادُواْ حَرَّمْنَا عَلَيْهِمْ طَيِّبَاتٍ أُحِلَّتْ لَهُمْ﴾.
This is made clear by His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿وَعَلَى الَّذِينَ هَادُوا حَرَّمْنَا كُلَّ ذِي ظُفُرٍ﴾ to the end of the verse.

nahhas-meani:162-162.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿لَّـٰكِنِ ٱلرَّاسِخُونَ فِي ٱلْعِلْمِ مِنْهُمْ وَٱلْمُؤْمِنُونَ يُؤْمِنُونَ بِمَآ أُنزِلَ إِلَيكَ وَمَآ أُنزِلَ مِن قَبْلِكَ﴾.
الراسخ: the firmly established; and "منهم" means the People of the Book.
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿وَٱلْمُقِيمِينَ ٱلصَّلاَةَ﴾.
And in it there is [the sense of praise, i.e. "and mention those who establish the prayer"].

nahhas-meani:163-163.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿إِنَّآ أَوْحَيْنَآ إِلَيْكَ كَمَآ أَوْحَيْنَآ إِلَىٰ نُوحٍ وَٱلنَّبِيِّينَ مِن بَعْدِهِ﴾.
This is connected to His saying: ﴿يَسْأَلُكَ أَهْلُ الْكِتَابِ أَنْ تُنَزِّلَ عَلَيْهِمْ كِتَابَاً مِنَ السَّمَاء﴾.
So Allah made known that his case is like the case of the prophets before him: revelation comes to him just as it came to them.
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَآتَيْنَا دَاوُودَ زَبُوراً﴾.
And it is read: ﴿زُبُوْرَاً﴾, with a ḍamma on the zāy.
Al-Kisāʾī said: Whoever reads ﴿زَبُوراً﴾, for him it is a singular, like "the Torah" and "the Gospel".
Someone else said: [It is of the pattern faʿūl] in the sense of mafʿūl (passive participle), just as one says ḥalūb in the sense of maḥlūb (milked); one says: زَبَرْتُهُ فهو مزبورٌ, i.e. "I wrote it," and "زَبُور" is in the sense of "مزبور" (written).
And whoever reads "زُبُوْراً", for him it is the plural of zabr.

nahhas-meani:164-164.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَكَلَّمَ ٱللَّهُ مُوسَىٰ تَكْلِيماً﴾.
It is emphatic (a mafʿūl muṭlaq, absolute object, for emphasis — [Translator's note: this gloss is added for clarity]); it indicates the meaning of speech as commonly known, because if you say "كَلَّمْتُ فلاناً" it may be that you conveyed your words to him (by some means), but if you say "كلَّمتُه تكليماً" it can only be speech of the kind that is known.
So Allah told of the special distinctions of the prophets, then told of what He singled out Moses ﷺ for.

nahhas-meani:166-166.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿لَّـٰكِنِ ٱللَّهُ يَشْهَدُ بِمَآ أَنزَلَ إِلَيْكَ أَنزَلَهُ بِعِلْمِهِ﴾.
Al-Qutabī said: "لَكِنْ" only occurs after a negation. He said: so it is construed according to the meaning, because when they denied (him) they had in effect negated, so He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿لَّـٰكِنِ ٱللَّهُ يَشْهَدُ بِمَآ أَنزَلَ إِلَيْكَ﴾.
Abū Jaʿfar said: This is a mistake, because "لَكِنْ", according to the grammarians, when a clause follows it, occurs after both negation and affirmation, and here a clause follows it; the grammarians say "it only occurs after a negation" only when a single word (mufrad) follows it.
And His saying ﴿أَنْزَلَهُ بِعِلْمِهِ﴾ means: He sent it down with His knowledge in it, just as you say "So-and-so came with the sword," i.e. with it on him; and just as He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿تَنْبُتُ بِالدُّهْنِ﴾.

nahhas-meani:172-172.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿لَّن يَسْتَنكِفَ ٱلْمَسِيحُ أَن يَكُونَ عَبْداً للَّهِ وَلاَ ٱلْمَلاۤئِكَةُ ٱلْمُقَرَّبُونَ﴾.
Qatāda said: "لن يستنكف": he will not feel ashamed (to do so).
And al-istinkāf according to the lexicographers is disdain; it is from نَكَفَ يَنْكِفُ, when someone removes a tear from his cheek with his hand.

nahhas-meani:174-174.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا ٱلنَّاسُ قَدْ جَآءَكُمْ بُرْهَانٌ مِّن رَّبِّكُمْ﴾.
Mujāhid said: A proof.
Sufyān said: By "the proof" He means the Prophet ﷺ.
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿وَأَنْزَلْنَآ إِلَيْكُمْ نُوراً مُّبِيناً﴾.
Qatāda said: It is the Qurʾān.
And according to the lexicographers it is a "figurative representation" (tamthīl), because the basic sense of light is that which makes things clear; so He likened what is known by the heart to what is seen with the eyes.

nahhas-meani:176-176.t: It is narrated from ʿAlqama that he said: "Everything in the Qurʾān that is ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ﴾ was revealed in Medina, and everything in the Qurʾān that is ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا ٱلنَّاسُ﴾ was revealed in Mecca."

nahhas-meani:49-49.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أَلَمْ تَرَ إِلَى ٱلَّذِينَ يُزَكُّونَ أَنْفُسَهُمْ بَلِ ٱللَّهُ يُزَكِّي مَن يَشَآءُ﴾.
The root of الزكاء is growth in righteousness.
Qatāda said: He means the Jews, because they declared themselves pure and said: we are the sons of Allah and His beloved ones.
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said likewise.
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿وَلاَ يُظْلَمُونَ فَتِيلاً﴾.
Ibn ʿAbbās said: الفتيل is what you roll between your two fingers.
Someone else said: الفتيل is what is in the groove of the date-stone.
النقير is the small pit in it, from which the palm sprouts.
القطمير is the husk wrapped around it on the outside.
The meaning is: they will not be wronged by the measure of this.

nahhas-meani:50-50.t:
Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿انظُرْ كَيفَ يَفْتَرُونَ عَلَى اللَّهِ الكَذِبَ﴾.
The meaning of ﴿يَفْتَرُوْنَ﴾ is: they fabricate and lie.

nahhas-meani:51-51.t:
His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿أَلَمْ تَرَ إِلَى ٱلَّذِينَ أُوتُواْ نَصِيباً مِّنَ ٱلْكِتَابِ يُؤْمِنُونَ بِٱلْجِبْتِ وَٱلطَّاغُوتِ﴾.
It is narrated from ʿUmar, may Allah have mercy on him, that he said: الجبت is sorcery and الطاغوت is Satan.
The like is narrated from al-Shaʿbī.
Qatāda said: الجبت is Satan and الطاغوت is the soothsayer.
It is narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās that الجبت and الطاغوت are two men of the Jews, namely "Kaʿb ibn al-Ashraf" and "Ḥuyayy ibn Akhṭab".
According to the linguists, الجبت and الطاغوت are anything worshipped besides Allah, or obeyed with an obedience involving disobedience to Allah, or submitted to.
These views are close to one another, because when they obeyed those two in disobedience to Allah and in disbelief in His prophets, they were in the position of one who worships them, as He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿اتَّخَذُوا أَحْبَارَهُمْ وَرُهْبَانَهُمْ أَرْبَابَاً مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ﴾.
Someone I trust narrated to me from Yūnus ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā, from Ibn Wahb, from Mālik, who said: الطاغوت is whatever is worshipped besides Allah.
From it is ﴿واجْتَنَبُوا الطَّاغُوتَ أَنْ يَعْبُدُوهَا﴾. I said to Mālik: what is الجبت? He said: I heard someone say: it is Satan.
This is supported by what Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad al-Azdī narrated to us; he said: Ibn Abī Dāwūd narrated to us; he said: al-Ḥimmānī narrated to us: Marwān ibn Muʿāwiya and Ibn al-Mubārak narrated to us from ʿAwf, from Ḥayyān ibn Qaṭan, from Qabīṣa ibn Mukhāriq, who said: I heard the Prophet ﷺ say: "Augury from birds (العيافة), taking ill omens (الطيرة) and divining by pebbles (الطرق) are of الجبت."
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿وَيَقُولُونَ لِلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ هَؤُلاءِ أَهْدَىٰ مِنَ ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ سَبِيلاً﴾.
Qatāda said: they are the Jews.
Someone else said: by this He makes clear that they were obstinate, because they said of those who worshipped idols and did not acknowledge any Book: these are better guided than [the believers] who affirmed the Books.

nahhas-meani:52-52.t:
His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿أُوْلَـٰئِكَ ٱلَّذِينَ لَعَنَهُمُ ٱللَّهُ﴾.
اللعنة is banishment, that is, He has distanced them from His granting of success (توفيق) and His mercy.

nahhas-meani:53-53.t:
His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿أَمْ لَهُمْ نَصِيبٌ مِّنَ ٱلْمُلْكِ﴾.
It is said: they were owners of orchards and wealth, and were miserly despite that.
And it is said: had they possessed sovereignty, they would have been miserly.

nahhas-meani:54-54.t:
His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿أَمْ يَحْسُدُونَ ٱلنَّاسَ عَلَىٰ مَآ آتَاهُمُ ٱللَّهُ مِن فَضْلِهِ فَقَدْ آتَيْنَآ آلَ إِبْرَاهِيمَ ٱلْكِتَابَ وَٱلْحِكْمَةَ﴾.
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: the Jews said: Muḥammad claims that [whatever he wishes] of women has been made lawful for him; so Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿أَمْ يَحْسُدُونَ ٱلنَّاسَ عَلَىٰ مَآ آتَاهُمُ ٱللَّهُ مِن فَضْلِهِ﴾. So the meaning is: rather, they envy the Prophet ﷺ for the women made lawful for him.
Al-Suddī said: Dāwūd, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, had a hundred wives, and Sulaymān more than that.
Qatāda said: those Jews envied this tribe of the Arabs when a prophet was sent among them; so «bounty» here is prophethood.
The Arabs were ennobled through the Prophet ﷺ; that is, how then do they not envy Ibrāhīm ﷺ and other prophets, when Sulaymān was given sovereignty?
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿وَآتَيْنَاهُمْ مُّلْكاً عَظِيماً﴾.
Mujāhid said: He means prophethood.
Hammām ibn al-Ḥārith said: they were supported by angels and armies.

nahhas-meani:55-55.t:
Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿فَمِنْهُمْ مَّنْ آمَنَ بِهِ وَمِنْهُمْ مَّن صَدَّ عَنْهُ﴾.
Mujāhid said: He means in the Qurʾān.
And it is said: in the Prophet ﷺ.
It is possible that the meaning is ﴿فمِنْهُمْ مَنْ آمَنَ﴾ in this report.
﴿وَمِنْهُمْ مَّن صَدَّ عَنْهُ وَكَفَىٰ بِجَهَنَّمَ سَعِيراً﴾; السعير is the intense blazing of the fire.

nahhas-meani:56-56.t:
His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ بِآيَاتِنَا سَوْفَ نُصْلِيهِمْ نَاراً﴾ [verse 56].
The meaning is: We cast them into it. One says: أَصْلَيْتُهُ إِصْلاءً when you cast him into the fire, as though you intend burning.
And صَلَيْتُ اللحمَ, when you roast it, أَصْلِيهِ صَلْياً.
And صَلِيتُ بالأمر أَصْلَى, when you endure its severity.
In the ḥadīth: a Jewish woman gave the Prophet ﷺ a مَصْلِيّة sheep, that is, a roasted one.
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿كُلَّمَا نَضِجَتْ جُلُودُهُمْ بَدَّلْنَاهُمْ جُلُوداً غَيْرَهَا﴾.
There are two views on this:
One of them: that the pain falls only upon the souls, and even if the skins are exchanged, the pain falls on the person.
The other view: that the first skin is restored anew, just as you say: I recast the ring.
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿لِيَذُوقُواْ ٱلْعَذَابَ﴾.
That is: so that the pain of the punishment reaches them.
* Then He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ كَانَ عَزِيزاً حَكِيماً﴾.
That is: He is wise in the punishment with which He has punished.

nahhas-meani:57-57.t:
His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ وَعَمِلُواْ ٱلصَّالِحَاتِ سَنُدْخِلُهُمْ جَنَّاتٍ تَجْرِي مِن تَحْتِهَا ٱلأَنْهَارُ﴾.
That is: the water of the rivers.
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿خَالِدِينَ فِيهَآ أَبَداً لَّهُمْ فِيهَآ أَزْوَاجٌ مُّطَهَّرَةٌ﴾.
That is: purified from impurities and menstruation.
* Then He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿وَنُدْخِلُهُمْ ظِـلاًّ ظَلِيلاً﴾.
That is: it shades from heat and cold, and not every shade is like that.

nahhas-meani:58-58.t:
His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَأْمُرُكُمْ أَن تُؤدُّواْ ٱلأَمَانَاتِ إِلَىۤ أَهْلِهَا﴾.
It is said, from Ibn ʿAbbās: this is general.
It is narrated from Shurayḥ that he said to one of two litigants: give him his right, for Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَأْمُرُكُمْ أَن تُؤدُّواْ ٱلأَمَانَاتِ إِلَىۤ أَهْلِهَا﴾.
Then Shurayḥ said: ﴿وَإنْ كَانَ ذُوْ عُسْرَةٍ فَنظِرَةٌ إِلَى مَيْسَرَةٍ﴾ — this concerns usury specifically.
And it is said: ﴿إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَأْمُرُكُمْ أَن تُؤدُّواْ ٱلأَمَانَاتِ إِلَىۤ أَهْلِهَا﴾ was revealed when the keys of the House were taken from "Shayba ibn ʿUthmān".
Ibn Zayd said: they are the rulers.
This view has been deemed good: that it is an address to those in charge of people's affairs, who were commanded to render the trust to those whose affairs they were put in charge of, and their rights, and what they were entrusted with of their affairs, and to act justly among them; so they were enjoined concerning the subjects.
Then He enjoined the subjects to obedience, saying, Majestic and Mighty is He, after it: ﴿يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا أَطِيعُوا اللَّهَ وَأَطِيعُوا الرَّسُولَ وَأُولِي الأَمْرِ مِنْكُمْ﴾.
However, Ibn ʿAbbās said: ﴿وَأُولُوا الأَمْرِ مِنْكُمْ﴾ — and those of jurisprudence and religion. «[Translator's note: the source quotes the phrase here as «وأولوا», in the nominative.]»
Mujāhid said: the Companions of Muḥammad.
Abū Hurayra said: they are the commanders.
This is among the best of them, except that it is in what agrees with the truth, as is authentically reported from the Prophet ﷺ: whoever commands disobedience is not to be obeyed.

nahhas-meani:59-59.t:
His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ أَطِيعُواْ ٱللَّهَ وَأَطِيعُواْ ٱلرَّسُولَ وَأُوْلِي ٱلأَمْرِ مِنْكُمْ﴾.
Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh said: those [in authority are those of jurisprudence and] knowledge.
Among the Successors, al-Ḥasan, Mujāhid and ʿAṭāʾ held this view.
Abū Hurayra said: He means by it the commanders of the military detachments.
Al-Suddī held this view.
It is strengthened by the fact that Abū Hurayra narrated from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: "Whoever obeys me has obeyed Allah, and whoever obeys my commander has obeyed me; whoever disobeys me has disobeyed Allah, and whoever disobeys my commander has disobeyed me."
ʿIkrima said: those in authority are Abū Bakr and ʿUmar.
All these views come back to one thing, because the commanders of the detachments were among the scholars, since none was appointed except one who had knowledge.
Likewise Abū Bakr and [ʿUmar were among] the scholars.
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿فَإِن تَنَازَعْتُمْ فِي شَيْءٍ فَرُدُّوهُ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ وَٱلرَّسُولِ﴾.
The derivation of المنازعة: that each of the two disputants pulls out (ينتزع) the argument for himself.
On His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿فَرُدُّوهُ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ وَٱلرَّسُولِ﴾ there are two views:
One of them, held by Mujāhid and Qatāda: refer it to the Book of Allah and the Sunna of His Messenger [and likewise ʿAmr ibn Maymūn said: refer it to the Book of Allah and His Messenger]; and when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ has died, refer it to his Sunna.
The other view: then say: Allah and His Messenger know best.
This is a stern warning concerning disagreement, because of His saying: ﴿إِن كُنْتُمْ تُؤْمِنُونَ بِٱللَّهِ وَٱلْيَوْمِ ٱلآخِرِ ذٰلِكَ خَيْرٌ وَأَحْسَنُ تَأْوِيلاً﴾.
Qatāda said: ﴿وَأَحْسَنُ تَأْوِيلاً﴾ means: and better in outcome.
This is better linguistically, and it would be from «آلَ إلى كذا» (it came to such-and-such).
It is possible that the meaning is: and better than your own interpretation.

nahhas-meani:60-60.t:
His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿أَلَمْ تَرَ إِلَى ٱلَّذِينَ يَزْعُمُونَ أَنَّهُمْ آمَنُواْ بِمَآ أُنْزِلَ إِلَيْكَ وَمَآ أُنزِلَ مِن قَبْلِكَ يُرِيدُونَ أَن يَتَحَاكَمُوۤاْ إِلَى ٱلطَّاغُوتِ﴾.
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: this was revealed concerning two men who disputed, one of them a Jew and the other a hypocrite. The Jew said: let Muḥammad judge between me and you; and the hypocrite said: let "Kaʿb ibn al-Ashraf" judge between me and you.

nahhas-meani:61-61.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَإِذَا قِيلَ لَهُمْ تَعَالَوْاْ إِلَىٰ مَآ أَنزَلَ ٱللَّهُ وَإِلَى ٱلرَّسُولِ رَأَيْتَ ٱلْمُنَافِقِينَ يَصُدُّونَ عَنكَ صُدُوداً﴾.
That is: they turn away from your judgement.

nahhas-meani:62-62.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَكَيْفَ إِذَآ أَصَابَتْهُمْ مُّصِيبَةٌ بِمَا قَدَّمَتْ أَيْدِيهِمْ﴾.
The meaning: ﴿فَكَيْفَ﴾ will their state be ﴿إِذَآ أَصَابَتْهُمْ مُّصِيبَةٌ بِمَا قَدَّمَتْ أَيْدِيهِمْ ثُمَّ جَآءُوكَ يَحْلِفُونَ بِٱللَّهِ إِنْ أَرَدْنَآ إِلاَّ إِحْسَاناً وَتَوْفِيقاً﴾.
It is narrated that ʿUmar killed the hypocrite who had said to the Jew: come with us to "Kaʿb ibn al-Ashraf" so that he may judge between us. Then his companions came to the Prophet ﷺ swearing by Allah: we intended nothing by seeking redress for the blood except good and conformity with the truth.
And it is said: the meaning is: when a punishment befell them it did not deter them, and they swore falsely that by seeking his judgement they intended nothing but good from one to another and what is right in it.

nahhas-meani:63-63.t:
Then He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿أُولَـٰئِكَ ٱلَّذِينَ يَعْلَمُ ٱللَّهُ مَا فِي قُلُوبِهِمْ﴾.
He knows everything; the point is that He knew they were hypocrites, so they were informed of that.
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿فَأَعْرِضْ عَنْهُمْ وَعِظْهُمْ وَقُل لَّهُمْ فِيۤ أَنْفُسِهِمْ قَوْلاً بَلِيغاً﴾.
That is: say to them: whoever opposes the judgement of the Prophet ﷺ and disbelieves in him, killing becomes obligatory upon him.

nahhas-meani:64-64.t:
His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَمَآ أَرْسَلْنَا مِن رَّسُولٍ إِلاَّ لِيُطَاعَ بِإِذْنِ ٱللَّهِ﴾.
(مِنْ) is redundant (zāʾida) for emphasis, and it indicates the sense of the genus.
The meaning of ﴿إِلاَّ بِإِذْنِ اللَّهِ﴾ «[Translator's note: so quoted in the source; the verse reads ﴿إِلاَّ لِيُطَاعَ بِإِذْنِ ٱللَّهِ﴾]» is: except by Allah having permitted it.
And it is said: its meaning may be: except by the knowledge of Allah.

nahhas-meani:65-65.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَلاَ وَرَبِّكَ لاَ يُؤْمِنُونَ حَتَّىٰ يُحَكِّمُوكَ فِيمَا شَجَرَ بَيْنَهُمْ﴾.
That is: in what they disagreed about; from it comes «تشاجر القوم» (the people quarrelled).
The origin of this is from الشجر (trees), because of the intertwining of its branches; from it comes «شجره بالرمح», that is, he lodged it in him like a branch in a tree; and from it comes «اشتجر القوم». Zuhayr said:
مَتَى يَشْتَجِرْ قَوْمٌ يَقُلْ سَرَوَاتُهُمْ * هُمُ بَيْنَنَا فُهْمٌ رضَىً، وهُمُ عَدْلُ
(Whenever a people quarrel, their nobles say: "They shall judge between us," for they are acceptable and they are just.)
His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿ثُمَّ لاَ يَجِدُواْ فِيۤ أَنْفُسِهِمْ حَرَجاً مِّمَّا قَضَيْتَ﴾.
That is: doubt and constriction.
The root of الحرج is constriction.
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿وَيُسَلِّمُواْ تَسْلِيماً﴾.
That is: and submit to your command; and His saying «تسليماً» is emphatic (muʾakkid).

nahhas-meani:69-69.t:
His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَمَن يُطِعِ ٱللَّهَ وَٱلرَّسُولَ فَأُوْلَـٰئِكَ مَعَ ٱلَّذِينَ أَنْعَمَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَيْهِم﴾.
It is narrated that some of the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ said: O Messenger of Allah, you are with us in this world, and on the Day of Resurrection you will be raised up because of your excellence. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿وَمَن يُطِعِ ٱللَّهَ وَٱلرَّسُولَ فَأُوْلَـٰئِكَ مَعَ ٱلَّذِينَ أَنْعَمَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَيْهِم مِّنَ ٱلنَّبِيِّينَ وَٱلصِّدِّيقِينَ وَٱلشُّهَدَآءِ وَٱلصَّالِحِينَ وَحَسُنَ أُولَـٰئِكَ رَفِيقاً﴾.
So He made known to them that those who are higher descend to those below them, and they gather together to recall the favours Allah bestowed upon them.

nahhas-meani:71-71.t:
His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ خُذُواْ حِذْرَكُمْ فَٱنفِرُواْ ثُبَاتٍ أَوِ ٱنْفِرُواْ جَمِيعاً﴾.
Qatāda said: الثبات are the parties.
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: الثبات are the bands, and الجميع are those gathered together.
The linguists said: الثبات are groups in separation.
The meaning is: go forth group after group, or go forth all together.
The singular of ثبات is ثُبَة, and it is derived from their saying «ثَبَّيْتُ الرجل» when you praise him during his lifetime, because it is as if you gathered together his good qualities.

nahhas-meani:72-72.t:
His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَإِنَّ مِنْكُمْ لَمَن لَّيُبَطِّئَنَّ فَإِنْ أَصَابَتْكُمْ مُّصِيبَةٌ قَالَ قَدْ أَنْعَمَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَيَّ﴾.
That is: he lags behind from fighting; «يبطّئ» is for intensiveness; the hypocrites are meant by it.
﴿فَإِنْ أَصَابَتْكُمْ مُّصِيبَةٌ﴾: that is, a defeat.
﴿ولئِنْ أَصَابَكُمْ فَضْلٌ مِنَ اللَّهِ﴾: that is, booty.
﴿لَيَقُولَنَّ كَأَنْ لَمْ تَكُنْ بَيْنَكُمْ وَبَيْنَهُ مَوَدَةٌ﴾ «[Translator's note: the word «الله» follows the quotation in the source.]»
Al-Ḥasan read «لَيَقُولُنَّ» with a ḍamma on the lām; this is construed according to the sense, «مَن» referring to a group. So this is parenthetical (muʿtariḍ).
The meaning is: «Allah has favoured me, since I was not present with them» ﴿كَأَنْ لَمْ يَكُنْ بَيْنَكُمْ وَبَيْنَهُ مَوَدَّة﴾, that is, as though he had not made a covenant with you for jihād.
It is possible that the meaning is: «Would that I had been with them so that I might attain a great triumph» — as though there had been no affection between you and him.

nahhas-meani:74-74.t:
His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿فَلْيُقَاتِلْ فِي سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ ٱلَّذِينَ يَشْرُونَ ٱلْحَيَاةَ ٱلدُّنْيَا بِٱلآخِرَةِ﴾.
The meaning of «يشرون» is: they sell. One says شريتُ الشيء when you sell it and when you buy it.
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿وَمَن يُقَاتِلْ فِي سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ فَيُقْتَلْ أَو يَغْلِبْ فَسَوْفَ نُؤْتِيهِ أَجْراً عَظِيماً﴾.
Muḥammad ibn al-Yamānī read: «فَيَقْتُلُ أو يَغْلِبُ».

nahhas-meani:75-75.t:
His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَمَا لَكُمْ لاَ تُقَاتِلُونَ فِي سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ وَٱلْمُسْتَضْعَفِينَ مِنَ ٱلرِّجَالِ وَٱلنِّسَآءِ وَٱلْوِلْدَانِ﴾.
Al-Zuhrī said: the meaning is: in the way of Allah and in the way of the oppressed.
Abū Jaʿfar said: Abū al-ʿAbbās said: it is possible that the meaning is: and for the oppressed.
And it is possible that the meaning is: and in the way of the oppressed.
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: these are people who accepted Islam but were unable to emigrate and remained in Mecca, so Allah, Majestic and Mighty, excused them.
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿ٱلَّذِينَ يَقُولُونَ رَبَّنَآ أَخْرِجْنَا مِنْ هَـٰذِهِ ٱلْقَرْيَةِ ٱلظَّالِمِ أَهْلُهَا﴾.
He means Mecca.

nahhas-meani:78-78.t:
His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿أَيْنَمَا تَكُونُواْ يُدْرِككُّمُ ٱلْمَوْتُ وَلَوْ كُنتُمْ فِي بُرُوجٍ مُّشَيَّدَةٍ﴾.
[Qatāda said: البروج are fortified palaces; and it is known in the language that] البروج are fortresses. المشيّدة bears two meanings:
1 - that they are made lofty.
2 - and the other: that they are plastered with الشِّيد, which is gypsum; ʿIkrima said likewise.
Al-Suddī said: they are white palaces built in the lowest heaven.
And it is said: المشيَّدة (with doubling) is the made-lofty, and المَشِيدة, without doubling, is that made with الشِّيد.
And it is said: المشيَّدة is for intensiveness, used for the plural.
His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَإِن تُصِبْهُمْ حَسَنَةٌ يَقُولُواْ هَـٰذِهِ مِنْ عِندِ ٱللَّهِ، وَإِن تُصِبْهُمْ سَيِّئَةٌ يَقُولُواْ هَـٰذِهِ مِنْ عِندِكَ﴾.
الحسنة here is fertility, and السيئة is drought.

nahhas-meani:79-79.t:
His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿مَّآ أَصَابَكَ مِنْ حَسَنَةٍ فَمِنَ ٱللَّهِ وَمَآ أَصَابَكَ مِن سَيِّئَةٍ فَمِن نَّفْسِكَ﴾.
﴿مِنْ حَسَنَةٍ﴾: that is, fertility. And it is said: this is addressed to the Prophet ﷺ, because addressing him is equivalent to addressing all people.
The meaning: ﴿مَّآ أَصَابَكَ مِنْ حَسَنَةٍ فَمِنَ ٱللَّهِ﴾, that is, of fertility and ease.
﴿وَمَآ أَصَابَكَ مِن سَيِّئَةٍ﴾: that is, of drought and hardship.
﴿فَمِن نَّفْسِكَ﴾: that is, it is a punishment for your sin; Qatāda said this.
It is narrated that the Jews said when the Muslims came to Medina:
drought has struck us and fertility has decreased.
So Allah, Majestic and Mighty, made known that this was because of their sins.
ʿAbd al-Wahhāb ibn Mujāhid narrated from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās, that he read: ﴿وَمَا أَصَابَكَ مِنْ سَيِّئَةٍ فَمِنْ نَفْسِكَ، وأنا كتبتها عليك﴾ (and I decreed it for you).
And it is said: the verb of saying is omitted, that is: they say this.

nahhas-meani:81-81.t:
His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَيَقُولُونَ طَاعَةٌ﴾.
The meaning is: and they say: our affair is obedience, and from us is obedience.
There is an ellipsis in the speech; the meaning is: and they say, when they are with you: obedience.
This is indicated by His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿فَإِذَا بَرَزُواْ مِنْ عِندِكَ بَيَّتَ طَآئِفَةٌ مِّنْهُمْ غَيْرَ ٱلَّذِي تَقُولُ﴾.
The meaning of (بَيَّتَ) according to the linguists is: he settled the matter by night and deliberated on it.
That is: he manifested the disobedience in his house; the Arabs say: «a matter settled (بُيِّت) by night» when it has been firmly decided. Night is singled out for this only because it is a time in which one is free.
The poet said:
أَجْمَعُوْا أَمْرَهُمْ بِلَيْلٍ فَلَمَّا * أَصْبَحُوْا أَصْبَحَتْ لَهُمْ ضَوْضَاءُ
(They resolved their affair by night, and when morning came, there arose an uproar among them.)
From this is: بَيَّتَّ الصيام (you made the intention to fast by night).
Abū Razīn said: the meaning of (بَيَّتَ) is: he composed.
This does not depart from the view of the linguists, because the composing may be by night.
And it is said: the meaning of (بَيَّتَ) is: he changed.
This is not sound.
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿وَٱللَّهُ يَكْتُبُ مَا يُبَيِّتُونَ﴾.
It bears two meanings:
One of them: that He sends it down in His Book and informs of it.
In that is the greatest of signs for the Prophet ﷺ, because he informs of what they keep secret.
And it may be that the meaning is: Allah knows and records what they plot by night.
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿فَأَعْرِضْ عَنْهُمْ وَتَوَكَّلْ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ وَكَفَىٰ بِٱللَّهِ وَكِيلاً﴾.
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: the hypocrites are meant by it.
The meaning is: do not disclose their names.

nahhas-meani:82-82.t:
His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿أَفَلاَ يَتَدَبَّرُونَ ٱلْقُرْآنَ﴾.
The meaning of «تدبّرتُ الشيء» is: I reflected on its outcome. One says «أدبر القوم» when their affair turned to its end. In the ḥadīth: "لا تدابروا", that is, do not be hostile to one another, that is, let none of you turn his back (دُبُر) on his fellow out of enmity.
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿وَلَوْ كَانَ مِنْ عِندِ غَيْرِ ٱللَّهِ لَوَجَدُواْ فِيهِ ٱخْتِلاَفاً كَثِيراً﴾.
That is: if what they are informed of — of what they keep secret — were from other than Allah, it would be inconsistent.
The position of Qatāda and Ibn Zayd is that the meaning is: if the Qurʾān were [from other than Allah, they would find in it disparity and contradiction], because people's speech varies and contradicts itself. «[Translator's note: the source has «يتناقص» (diminishes), evidently for «يتناقض» (contradicts itself); translated per the evident sense.]»

nahhas-meani:83-83.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَإِذَا جَآءَهُمْ أَمْرٌ مِّنَ ٱلأَمْنِ أَوِ ٱلْخَوْفِ أَذَاعُواْ بِهِ﴾.
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: they spread it and went about with it; they are the hypocrites.
Someone else said: they are the weak among the Muslims; when they heard the hypocrites spreading the news of the Prophet ﷺ, they imagined there was no harm upon them in that, so they spread it. Allah reproached them for that and said: ﴿وَلَوْ رَدُّوهُ إِلَى ٱلرَّسُولِ وَإِلَىٰ أُوْلِي ٱلأَمْرِ مِنْهُمْ﴾, that is, those of knowledge, ﴿لَعَلِمَهُ ٱلَّذِينَ يَسْتَنْبِطُونَهُ مِنْهُمْ﴾, that is, who extract it.
One says «نبطتُ البئر» when you draw out from it the نَبَط, which is what comes out of it; from this the Nabaṭ were named, because they bring out water in the land.
So the meaning is: they would know what ought to be spread and what ought to be concealed.
* His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَلَوْلاَ فَضْلُ ٱللَّهِ عَلَيْكُمْ وَرَحْمَتُهُ لاَتَّبَعْتُمُ ٱلشَّيْطَانَ إِلاَّ قَلِيلاً﴾.
In this verse there are three views:
One of them: that the meaning is: were it not for what Allah bestowed of what He made clear and commanded, you would have followed Satan, except a few.
The other view: that the meaning is: they spread it, except a few.
This view is al-Kisāʾī's, and it is sound, from Ibn ʿAbbās.
And the other view, the view of Qatāda and Ibn Jurayj, which Abū Isḥāq used to prefer: that the meaning is: those of them who extract it would know it, except a few.
﴿وَلَوْلاَ فَضْلُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْكُمْ وَرَحْمَتُهُ لاَتَّبَعْتُمُ الشَّيْطَانَ﴾.
It is said: it is an exception from ﴿لاَتَّبَعْتُمُ الشَّيْطَانَ﴾.
By it are meant people who had not intended what the others intended of following Satan, as al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: they are the Companions of the Prophet, upon him be peace; ﴿إِلاَّ قَلِيلاً﴾: except a group of them.
And it is said: the meaning of ﴿إِلاَّ قَلِيلاً﴾ is: all of you.
Abū Jaʿfar said: this is not known in the language.
Among the best of these views is the view of the one who said: they spread it, except a few; because it is far-fetched that the meaning be: those of them who extract it would know it, except a few — for once it has been made clear, all are equal in knowing it, so excepting some of those who extract it is far-fetched.

nahhas-meani:84-84.t:
Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿فَقَاتِلْ فِي سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ لاَ تُكَلَّفُ إِلاَّ نَفْسَكَ﴾.
This is connected with His saying: ﴿وَمَا لَكُمْ لاَ تُقَاتِلُوْنَ فِي سَبِيْلِ اللَّهِ﴾. So Allah, Majestic and Mighty, commanded him to fight even if he were alone, because He had promised him victory.
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿عَسَى ٱللَّهُ أَن يَكُفَّ بَأْسَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ﴾.
البأس is might.
﴿عَسَى﴾ from Allah is binding, because it is for hope; so when He commands that something be hoped for, it comes to be.

nahhas-meani:85-85.t:
His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿مَّن يَشْفَعْ شَفَاعَةً حَسَنَةً يَكُنْ لَّهُ نَصِيبٌ مِّنْهَا﴾.
Al-Ḥasan said: whoever intercedes is rewarded even if his intercession is not accepted, because He, Majestic and Mighty, said ﴿مَّن يَشْفَعْ﴾ and did not say «whoever has his intercession accepted (مَن يُشَفَّع)».
Abū Mūsā al-Ashʿarī, may Allah have mercy on him, said: we were with the Prophet ﷺ when a beggar came, and the Prophet ﷺ said: "Intercede and you will be rewarded, and Allah decrees upon the tongue of His Prophet whatever He wills."
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿وَمَن يَشْفَعْ شَفَاعَةً سَيِّئَةً يَكُنْ لَّهُ كِفْلٌ مِّنْهَا﴾.
It is narrated from Abū Mūsā that he said: الكفل is the portion — or he said: the share — so it is in the ḥadīth.
Qatāda said: الكفل is the sin.
What is known among the linguists is that الكفل is the portion. One says: «اكتفلتُ البعير» when you put a cloak or the like on a part of it so as to ride it.
This is taken from that, because you only put it on a portion of the like of it.
* His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَكَانَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ مُّقِيتاً﴾.
There are two views on its meaning:
Muʿāwiya ibn Ṣāliḥ narrated from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥa, from Ibn ʿAbbās: ﴿مَقِيتَاً﴾,
he says: guardian.
And with his chain: ﴿مقيتاً﴾, he says: powerful.
Al-Kisāʾī related that he said: أقات يُقيت, when one has power.
The poet said:
وَذِي ضِعْنٍ كَفَفْتُ النَّفْسَ عَنْهُ * وكُنْتُ عَلَى مَسَاءَتِهِ مُقِيتَاً
(Many a rancorous man have I held myself back from, though I had power to do him harm.)
And the other view is that المقيت is the guardian.
Abū Isḥāq said: this view is in my opinion more correct than that, because it is taken from القوت (sustenance), and القوت is the amount that preserves a person.
The poet said:
أَلِيَ الفَضْلُ أمْ عليَّ إذا حُوْ * سِبْتُ إنِّي عَلَى الحِسَابِ مُقِيتُ
(Is the surplus in my favour or against me when I am brought to account? I am watchful over the reckoning.)
In the ḥadīth: "It is sin enough for a man to neglect the one he يُقيت",
that is, he preserves.
It is also narrated: «يَقُوت» (he feeds).

nahhas-meani:86-86.t:
His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَإِذَا حُيِّيتُم بِتَحِيَّةٍ فَحَيُّواْ بِأَحْسَنَ مِنْهَآ أَوْ رُدُّوهَآ﴾.
It is said: this concerns the greeting of peace. When one says «peace be upon you», reply to him: «and upon you be peace and the mercy of Allah». And when one says «peace be upon you [and the mercy of Allah]»,
it is said: «and upon you be peace and the mercy of Allah and His blessings».
The Shaykh Abū Bakr said: I found in a copy other than mine: and when one says «peace be upon you and the mercy of Allah and His blessings», reply to him: «and upon you».
This is narrated from the Prophet ﷺ.
It is narrated from al-Ḥasan that he said: the greeting is a sunna and returning it is an obligation.
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ كَانَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ حَسِيباً﴾.
Mujāhid said: that is, guardian.
الحسيب according to [some of] the Basran linguists is: the one who suffices.
One says «أحسبه» when he sufficed him; from it: ﴿عَطَاءً حِسَابَاً﴾,
and from it: حَسْبُك (enough for you).
In my view this is a mistake, because in this sense one does not say «أحسب على الشيء فهو حسيب عليه»; it is only said without «على».
The correct view is that it is from الحساب (reckoning): one says «حاسب فلاناً على كذا», and he is his reckoner over it, and his حسيب, that is, the one in charge of his reckoning.

nahhas-meani:87-87.t:
His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿ٱللَّهُ لاۤ إِلَـٰهَ إِلاَّ هُوَ لَيَجْمَعَنَّكُمْ إِلَىٰ يَوْمِ ٱلْقِيَامَةِ لاَ رَيْبَ فِيهِ﴾.
It is said: it is called القيامة only because people stand (يقومون) for the Lord of the worlds, that is, the day of standing (القيام); then the هاء was added for intensiveness.
And it is said: that is only because people rise from their graves, as He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿يَخْرُجُوْنَ مِنَ الأَجْدَاْثِ سِرَاْعَاً﴾; الأجداث are the graves.

nahhas-meani:88-88.t:
His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿فَمَا لَكُمْ فِي ٱلْمُنَافِقِينَ فِئَتَيْنِ﴾.
That is: two differing parties.
Zayd ibn Thābit said: some people stayed behind from the Prophet ﷺ on the day of Uḥud, and the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ became two parties: some of them said: kill them, and some said: pardon them. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿فَمَا لَكُم فِي المُنَافِقِينَ فِئَتَيْنِ﴾.
Mujāhid said: they were people who accepted Islam, then asked the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, for permission to go out to Mecca to fetch goods of theirs. The Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ became two parties regarding them: some saying they are hypocrites, and some saying they are believers — until we ascertained that they were hypocrites. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿فَمَا لَكُمْ فِي ٱلْمُنَافِقِينَ فِئَتَيْنِ وَٱللَّهُ أَرْكَسَهُمْ بِمَا كَسَبُوۤاْ﴾.
It is narrated from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd that he read (رَكَسَهُمْ) without alif. One says أركسهم and ركسهم when he turned them back.
The meaning is: He returned them to the ruling of the unbelievers.
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿أَتُرِيدُونَ أَن تَهْدُواْ مَنْ أَضَلَّ ٱللَّهُ﴾? [verse 88].
That is: they have gone astray.
﴿وَمَن يُضْلِلِ ٱللَّهُ فَلَن تَجِدَ لَهُ سَبِيلاً﴾: that is, a straight path.

nahhas-meani:1-1.t:
Among that is His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يٰأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّاسُ ٱتَّقُواْ رَبَّكُمُ ٱلَّذِي خَلَقَكُمْ مِّن نَّفْسٍ وَاحِدَةٍ وَخَلَقَ مِنْهَا زَوْجَهَا﴾.
Mujāhid said: Eve was created from Adam's lowest rib (quṣayrā).
And in the ḥadīth: "Woman was created from a crooked rib."
It has also been said: ﴿منها﴾ means: of its kind.
* Then He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿وَبَثَّ مِنْهُمَا رِجَالاً كَثِيراً وَنِسَآءً﴾.
One says: bathathtu the thing and abthathtuhu, when I spread it out. From it is:
﴿كَالْفَرَاشِ الْمَبْثُوثِ﴾.
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَٱتَّقُواْ ٱللَّهَ ٱلَّذِي تَسَآءَلُونَ بِهِ وَٱلأَرْحَامَ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ كَانَ عَلَيْكُمْ رَقِيباً﴾.
ʿIkrima said: The meaning is: and fear [Allah regarding] the wombs (ties of kinship), lest you sever them.
Ibrāhīm said: It is from their saying: [I ask you by Allah] and by the womb (kinship).
Abū Jaʿfar said: This is according to the reading of whoever read it with the genitive (khafḍ) [وَٱلأَرْحَامِ].
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَآتُوْا اليَتَامَى أَمْوَالَهُمْ وَلاَ تَتَبَدَّلُوا الخَبِيثَ بِالطَّيَّبِ﴾.
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: Do not give them counterfeit coins in exchange for good ones.
Someone else said: Do not exchange the unlawful for the lawful.

nahhas-meani:2-2.t:
Then He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿وَلاَ تَأْكُلُوۤاْ أَمْوَالَهُمْ إِلَىٰ أَمْوَالِكُمْ﴾.
It has been said: the meaning is [together with your wealth. The better view is that ﴿إِلَىٰ﴾ is in its own proper sense, and the meaning is]: and do not join their wealth to your wealth.
Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿إِنَّهُ كَانَ حُوباً كَبِيراً﴾.
Qatāda said: al-ḥūb is: sin.
It is related that Abū Ayyūb divorced his wife, or resolved to divorce her, and the Prophet ﷺ said: "The divorce of Umm Ayyūb is indeed a sin (ḥūb)."

nahhas-meani:3-3.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَإِنْ خِفْتُمْ أَلاَّ تُقْسِطُواْ فِي ٱلْيَتَامَىٰ﴾.
One says: aqsaṭa the man, when he acted justly, and qasaṭa, when he acted unjustly.
So it is as though "aqsaṭa" removed the injustice (qusūṭ).
As for the meaning of ﴿وَإِنْ خِفْتُمْ أَلاَّ تُقْسِطُواْ فِي ٱلْيَتَامَىٰ فَٱنكِحُواْ مَا طَابَ لَكُمْ مِّنَ ٱلنِّسَآءِ﴾ — [Translator's note: the text does not state "there are two views" here, but proceeds directly to "one of them".]
One of them: that Ibn ʿAbbās said, according to what is related from him: A man was restricted to four [wives] on account of the orphans.
An explanation of this view is related from a group of the Successors (tābiʿūn).
It is related from Mujāhid, al-Ḍaḥḥāk and Qatāda, and this is the meaning of what they said:
The Muslims used to ask about the matter of the orphans when strictness was imposed regarding it, so He, Majestic and Mighty is He, said: ﴿وَإِنْ خِفْتُمْ أَلاَّ تُقْسِطُواْ فِي ٱلْيَتَامَىٰ﴾.
That is: just as you fear regarding the matter of the orphans, so fear, regarding the matter of women when they are combined [in marriage], that you will be unable to be just among them.
The other view: al-Zuhrī related it from ʿUrwa, from ʿĀʾisha. He said: I asked ʿĀʾisha about the saying of Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He, ﴿وَإِنْ خِفْتُمْ أَلاَّ تُقْسِطُواْ فِي ٱلْيَتَامَىٰ فَٱنكِحُواْ مَا طَابَ لَكُمْ مِّنَ ٱلنِّسَآءِ﴾, and she said: O son of my sister, it is the orphan girl who is in the care of her guardian; her wealth and her beauty please him, and he wants to marry her without being just in her dower, giving her the like of what someone else would give her.
So they were forbidden to marry the orphan girls if they feared [injustice], and four of the women were made lawful for them. ʿĀʾisha said: [Then] the people asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ for a ruling after this verse, so Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, revealed ﴿وَيَسْتَفْتُونَكَ فِيْ النِّسَاءِ قُلِ اللـهُ يُفْتِيْكُمْ فِيْهِنَّ﴾ up to His saying ﴿وَتَرْغَبُونَ أَنْ تَنْكِحُوْهُنَّ﴾. She said: And what Allah mentioned as being recited to you in the Book is the first verse, in which is ﴿فَٱنكِحُواْ مَا طَابَ لَكُمْ مِّنَ ٱلنِّسَآءِ﴾. She said: And His saying ﴿وَتَرغَبُونَ أَنْ تَنْكِحُوهُنَّ﴾ is the aversion of one of you to his orphan girl who is in his care, when she has little wealth and beauty; so they were forbidden to marry those of the orphan women whose wealth and beauty they desired, except with justice, because of their aversion to them.
And the people of reasoned investigation (ahl al-naẓar) hold [this] view.
"Abū al-ʿAbbās" Muḥammad ibn Yazīd said: The implied construction (taqdīr) is: and if you fear that you will not be just in marrying the orphan girls; then this was omitted, and ﴿فَٱنكِحُواْ﴾ indicates it.
A group of the linguists held the first view, among them "al-Farrāʾ" and "Ibn Qutayba".
The second view has a higher isnad and is better according to the people of reasoned investigation.
As for whoever says that the meaning of ﴿مَثْنَىٰ وَثُلاَثَ وَرُبَاعَ﴾ is nine, no attention is paid to what he says, and it is not sound in the language, because the meaning of (مثنى) according to the experts in Arabic is: two and two, not just two.
Moreover, concision is part of the speech of the Arabs, and it cannot mean nine, because if it meant nine, saying "marry two, three and four" would not be concise, since "nine" is more concise than this.
Moreover, if it were according to this view, it would not be lawful for anyone to marry except nine or one; so the falsity of this has become clear.
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ذٰلِكَ أَدْنَىٰ أَلاَّ تَعُولُواْ﴾.
﴿أَدْنَىٰ﴾ is in the sense of: nearer.
ʿUmar ibn Muḥammad related from Hishām ibn ʿUrwa, from his father, from ʿĀʾisha, from the Prophet ﷺ, concerning His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He, ﴿ذٰلِكَ أَدْنَىٰ أَلاَّ تَعُولُواْ﴾, that he said: "That you not act unjustly."
Ibn ʿAbbās, al-Ḥasan, Abū Mālik, Mujāhid, ʿIkrima, Qatāda and al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: the meaning of ﴿أَنْ لاَ تَعُولُواْ﴾ is: that you not deviate.
Abū al-ʿAbbās said — concerning the view of whoever said that ﴿أَنْ لاَ تَعُولُواْ﴾ is from ʿiyāl (dependants) —: This is false and mistaken, because He has made lawful of those whom the right hand possesses whatever number there may be, and they are among those who are supported as dependants.
Moreover, He mentioned only women and what is lawful of them, and justice and injustice among them; so "أَنْ لاَ تَعُولُوا" in the sense of dependants has no meaning here. According to the view of the exegetes it is: that you not deviate and not act unjustly. From it is: "the inheritance-share ʿālat", when the shares exceed [the estate] so that whoever has a fixed share receives less; and from it: "my muʿawwala is on So-and-so", i.e. I incline to him and go far in that; and from it: "the thing ʿālanī", when it exceeded the measure; and from it: "So-and-so yuʿawwilu (wails)", and al-ʿawīl (wailing) is in fact going beyond [bounds].
Moreover, one only says aʿāla the man, yuʿīlu, when his dependants have become many.

nahhas-meani:4-4.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَآتُواْ ٱلنِّسَآءَ صَدُقَاتِهِنَّ نِحْلَةً﴾.
It has been said: the husbands are meant by it.
It is related that the guardian used to take the dower for himself, so Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, commanded that it be paid to the women; this is the view of Abū Ṣāliḥ.
Abū al-ʿAbbās said: The meaning of ﴿نِحْلَةً﴾ is that it would have been permissible that they not be given any of it, but Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, granted it to them as a gift (naḥalahunna).
It has been said: the meaning of (نِحْلَةً) is: religion, from their saying "So-and-so yantaḥilu such-and-such" (professes it), i.e. as an act of devotion ordained by Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He.
It has been said: an obligation; and the meaning is the same, because an obligation is something by which one worships.
It has also been said: (نِحْلَةً) is only what the soul is pleased to give; as for what one is compelled to give, it is not (نِحْلَةً).
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَإِن طِبْنَ لَكُمْ عَن شَيْءٍ مِّنْهُ نَفْساً فَكُلُوهُ هَنِيئاً مَّرِيئاً﴾.
He means: the dower.
That is: with no turbidity in it.
One says: amraʾanī the thing, with the alif; but when you say "hanaʾanī wa-maraʾanī" — this is the position of [most of] the linguists — they say it [without alif] for the sake of harmony (itbāʿ).
As for Abū al-ʿAbbās, he said: One only says amraʾanī for the good [thing], so as to distinguish between it and the supplication.
And al-murūʾa (manliness) is from this, because its possessor takes upon himself burdensome matters whose outcome he finds wholesome.

nahhas-meani:5-5.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلاَ تُؤْتُواْ ٱلسُّفَهَآءَ أَمْوَالَكُمُ ٱلَّتِي جَعَلَ ٱللَّهُ لَكُمْ قِيَاماً﴾.
ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar and a group of the Successors said: al-sufahāʾ are: women and children.
They only said so because foolishness is more common among these.
Al-safah is: ignorance, and its origin is: lightness. One says: "a safīh garment", when it is light (flimsy). The sinner is called safīh because he has no standing among the believers; he is light in their eyes and of little account to them.
The meaning is: and do not give the foolish more than they need, lest they squander it.
The proof of this is His saying afterwards: ﴿وَٱرْزُقُوهُمْ فِيهَا وَٱكْسُوهُمْ وَقُولُواْ لَهُمْ قَوْلاً مَّعْرُوفاً﴾, i.e. teach them the matter of their religion.

nahhas-meani:6-6.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَٱبْتَلُواْ ٱلْيَتَامَىٰ حَتَّىٰ إِذَا بَلَغُواْ النِّكَاحَ﴾.
Al-Ḥasan said: That is, test them.
* And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿فَإِنْ آنَسْتُمْ مِّنْهُمْ رُشْداً﴾.
"آنستم" is in the sense of: you know and perceive; and from it is the poet's saying:
آنَسَتْ نَبْأَةً وَأَفْزَعَها القَنَّا * صُ عَصْرَاً وَقَدْ دَنَا الإِمْسَاءُ
(She perceived a faint sound, and the hunters startled her in the late afternoon, when evening had drawn near.)
Al-rushd is: the straight path.
Mujāhid said: [It is] intelligence.
Sufyān said: Intelligence, and the safeguarding of wealth.
Abū Jaʿfar said: This is one of the best things said about it, because the people of knowledge are agreed that if he is intelligent and acts soundly, he is not among those who deserve to be placed under interdiction (ḥajr) regarding his wealth.
* Then He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿فَٱدْفَعُواْ إِلَيْهِمْ أَمْوَالَهُمْ وَلاَ تَأْكُلُوهَآ إِسْرَافاً وَبِدَاراً أَن يَكْبَرُواْ﴾.
That is: in haste, before they grow up and take it from you.
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمَن كَانَ غَنِيّاً فَلْيَسْتَعْفِفْ وَمَن كَانَ فَقِيراً فَلْيَأْكُلْ بِٱلْمَعْرُوفِ﴾.
There are several views on this verse:
The best of them is that the guardian of the orphan may take of it, if he is poor, as much as sustains him.
Likewise it is related from ʿUmar that he said: I am, with respect to this wealth, in the position of the guardian of an orphan; he takes from it what suits his needs when he is in need.
Al-Qāsim ibn Muḥammad related that a Bedouin asked Ibn ʿAbbās: What is lawful for me of my orphan's wealth? He allowed him to take from it, if he served him, so long as he was not extravagant.
ʿAbīda, al-Shaʿbī and Abū al-ʿĀliya said: He may not take anything except as a loan.
ʿUmar ibn Ismāʿīl ibn Abī Ghaylān narrated to us, saying: Dāwūd al-Ḍabbī narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Mubārak narrated to us, from ʿĀṣim, from Abū al-ʿĀliya: ﴿وَمَن كَانَ فَقِيراً فَلْيَأْكُلْ بِٱلْمَعْرُوفِ﴾ — he said: as a loan. Then he recited this verse: ﴿فَإِذَا دَفَعْتُمْ إِلَيْهِمْ أَمْوَالَهُمْ فَأَشْهِدُواْ عَلَيْهِمْ﴾.
Abū Yaḥyā said, from Mujāhid: He may not take a loan or anything else.
Of the jurists, Abū Yūsuf held this view, and he took the position [that] the verse is abrogated, abrogated by His saying ﴿يَا أَيُّها الَّذِينَ آمَنُوْا لاَ تَأْكُلُواْ أَمْوَالكُمْ بَيْنَكُمْ بِالبَاطِلِ إِلاَّ أَنْ تَكُوْنَ تِجَارَةً﴾ — and this is not trade.

nahhas-meani:7-7.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لِّلرِّجَالِ نَصيِبٌ مِّمَّا تَرَكَ ٱلْوَالِدَانِ وَٱلأَقْرَبُونَ وَلِلنِّسَآءِ نَصِيبٌ مِّمَّا تَرَكَ ٱلْوَالِدَانِ وَٱلأَقْرَبُونَ﴾.
It is related that they used not to let women inherit, saying: None inherits except one who has thrust with the spear and fought with the sword. So Allah revealed ﴿وَلِلنِّسَآءِ نَصِيبٌ مِّمَّا تَرَكَ ٱلْوَالِدَانِ وَٱلأَقْرَبُونَ مِمَّا قَلَّ مِنْهُ أَوْ كَثُرَ نَصِيباً مَّفْرُوضاً﴾.

nahhas-meani:8-8.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَإِذَا حَضَرَ ٱلْقِسْمَةَ أُوْلُواْ ٱلْقُرْبَىٰ وَٱلْيَتَامَىٰ وَٱلْمَسَاكِينُ﴾.
There are several views on this verse:
One of them: that it is abrogated.
Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab said: Inheritance and bequest abrogated it.
The consensus of most scholars at this time is that giving to them is not obligatory; this is only by way of encouragement to do good.
That is: if they are present, give to them, just as the deceased used to be commanded to give to them.
ʿAbīda, al-Shaʿbī, al-Zuhrī and al-Ḥasan said: It is unabrogated (muḥkama).
Ibn Abī Najīḥ said: They must be given what the souls are pleased to give.
Abū Jaʿfar said: And that this be in gratitude for what Allah has provided them with, to the exclusion of him.
* Then He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿وَقُولُواْ لَهُمْ قَوْلاً مَّعْرُوفاً﴾.
Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said: It is said to them: Take, may it be blessed for you.

nahhas-meani:9-9.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلْيَخْشَ ٱلَّذِينَ لَوْ تَرَكُواْ مِنْ خَلْفِهِمْ ذُرِّيَّةً ضِعَافاً خَافُواْ عَلَيْهِمْ﴾.
Saʿīd ibn Jubayr and Mujāhid said: [It is] about the man who is present with a sick person and says to him: Send forward some good, or give charity to your relatives. So they were commanded to have compassion for the sick man's heirs, just as they have compassion for their own heirs.
Miqsam said: The one who is present with him says to him: Fear Allah, and keep your wealth for yourself, for no one has more right to your wealth than your children — whereas had they been relatives of the one making the bequest, they would have loved him to make a bequest to their children.
The view of Saʿīd ibn Jubayr is closer to the meaning of the verse, and Allah knows best.
Because the meaning is: they feared poverty for them; so the fear falls upon the offspring of the dead.

nahhas-meani:10-10.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ يَأْكُلُونَ أَمْوَالَ ٱلْيَتَامَىٰ ظُلْماً﴾.
Al-yatīm in the language is: the one left alone. So a human being whose father has died is called yatīm; and among animals it is the one whose mother has died.
* And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿إِنَّمَا يَأْكُلُونَ فِي بُطُونِهِمْ نَاراً وَسَيَصْلَوْنَ سَعِيراً﴾.
This is figurative (majāz) in the wording; its literal reality in the language is that, since what they eat leads them to the Fire, they are in the position of one who eats fire, even though they are eating good things.

nahhas-meani:90-90.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِلاَّ ٱلَّذِينَ يَصِلُونَ إِلَىٰ قَوْمٍ بَيْنَكُمْ وَبَيْنَهُمْ مِّيثَاقٌ﴾.
Mujāhid said: they went over to "Hilāl ibn ʿUwaymir", and there was an alliance between him and the Prophet.
Someone else said: there were people who made a truce with the Prophet ﷺ and did not fight him, so the Muslims were commanded not to fight whoever went over to them, joined them, and made a truce as they had made a truce.
Abū ʿUbayda said: the meaning of ﴿يَصِلُونَ﴾ is: they trace their lineage to them.
This is a mistake, because the Prophet ﷺ fought Quraysh, and they were kinsmen of the first Emigrants.
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿أَوْ جَآءُوكُمْ حَصِرَتْ صُدُورُهُمْ﴾.
That is: or they reach a people who have come to you, their breasts constricted.
Al-Kisāʾī said: the meaning of (حَصِرَتْ) is: became constricted.
Mujāhid said: it is "Hilāl ibn ʿUwaymir", who was reluctant to fight the Muslims or to fight his own people, and so defended them.
Abū al-ʿAbbās Muḥammad ibn Yazīd said: the meaning is by way of imprecation, that is: may Allah constrict their breasts.
Abū Isḥāq said: it may be a khabar (predicate) after a khabar; so the meaning is ﴿أَوْ جَآءُوكُمْ﴾, then He gave a further statement after it and said: ﴿حَصِرَتْ صُدُورُهُمْ﴾, as He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿إِنَّ مَثَلَ عِيسَى عِنْدَ اللَّهِ كَمَثَلِ آدَمَ خَلَقَهُ مِنْ تُرَابٍ﴾.
And it is said: the meaning is: or they came to you, their breasts having become (قد) constricted; then قد was omitted.
Al-Ḥasan read: ﴿حَصِرَةً صُدُورُهُمْ﴾.
It is narrated from Ubayy ibn Kaʿb that he read: ﴿إلاَّ الَّذِينَ يَصِلُونَ إلَى قَوْمٍ﴾ [بيْنَكُمْ وبينهم ميثاق وحصرتْ صدورهم]; so the meaning according to this reading is ﴿إلاَّ الَّذِينَ يَصِلُونَ إلَى قَوْمٍ بَيْنَكُمْ وبَيْنَهُمْ مِيثَاقٌ وحَصِرتْ صُدُورهُمْ﴾,
that is: a people whose breasts are حَصِرة, that is, constricted.
His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿فَإِنِ ٱعْتَزَلُوكُمْ فَلَمْ يُقَاتِلُوكُمْ﴾.
That is: they refrained from fighting you.
﴿وَأَلْقَوْاْ إِلَيْكُمُ ٱلسَّلَمَ﴾:
that is, submission.
﴿فَمَا جَعَلَ ٱللَّهُ لَكُمْ عَلَيْهِمْ سَبِيلاً﴾.
Qatāda said: this verse is abrogated; it was abrogated by ﴿فَاقْتُلُوْا الْمُشْرِكِيْنَ حَيْثُ وَجَدْتُمُوْهُمْ﴾ in Barāʾa.

nahhas-meani:91-91.t:
His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿سَتَجِدُونَ آخَرِينَ يُرِيدُونَ أَن يَأْمَنُوكُمْ وَيَأْمَنُواْ قَوْمَهُمْ كُلَّ مَا رُدُّوۤاْ إِلَى ٱلْفِتْنِةِ أُرْكِسُواْ فِيِهَا﴾.
Mujāhid said: these were people of Mecca who would come to the Prophet ﷺ and accept Islam, then return to the unbelievers and relapse into idol-worship.
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿فَإِن لَّمْ يَعْتَزِلُوكُمْ وَيُلْقُوۤاْ إِلَيْكُمُ ٱلسَّلَمَ وَيَكُفُّوۤاْ أَيْدِيَهُمْ فَخُذُوهُمْ وَٱقْتُلُوهُمْ حَيْثُ ثَقِفْتُمُوهُمْ﴾.
The meaning of ﴿ثَقِفْتُمُوْهُمْ﴾ and «وجدتموهم» (you found them) is one.
﴿وَأُوْلَـٰئِكُمْ جَعَلْنَا لَكُمْ عَلَيْهِمْ سُلْطَاناً مُّبِيناً﴾:
that is, a clear proof that they are treacherous, not keeping any covenant or truce.

nahhas-meani:92-92.t:
His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَمَا كَانَ لِمُؤْمِنٍ أَن يَقْتُلَ مُؤْمِناً إِلاَّ خَطَئاً﴾.
This is an exception not of the same kind as what precedes.
Abū Isḥāq said: the meaning is: it is not for a believer to kill a believer at all; then He said ﴿إِلاَّ خَطَئاً﴾, [that is]: but if he kills him by mistake.
Whoever says that ﴿إلا﴾ is in the sense of «و» (and), his view is a mistake in two respects:
One of them: that it is not known for (إلا) to be in the sense of a conjunction.
The other respect: that a mistake cannot be restricted, because it is not something intended; if it were intended, it would be deliberate.
Sībawayh mentioned that (إلاَّ) frequently comes in the sense of (لكن) (but), and he recited:
مَنْ كانَ أسَرعَ في تَفَرُّقِ فَالجٍ * فَلَبُونُهُ جَرِبتْ مَعَاً وأُغَدَّتِ
إِلاَّ كَنَـا شِـرَةَ الذَّي ضيَّعتُمُ * كالغُصْن في غُلَوَائِهِ المتَنَبّتِ
(Whoever was quickest in scattering the tribe of Fālij — may his milch-camels all be stricken with mange and plague; but not like Nāshira, whom you let perish, who was like the branch growing in the fullness of its youth.)
The cause of the revelation of this verse, according to what Ibn Abī Najīḥ narrated from Mujāhid, was that "ʿAyyāsh ibn Abī Rabīʿa", the maternal half-brother of Abū Jahl, killed a believing man who used to torment him, along with Abū Jahl, for following the Prophet ﷺ; he reckoned that he was still an unbeliever as he had been, and so killed him.
* His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَمَن قَتَلَ مُؤْمِناً خَطَئاً فَتَحْرِيرُ رَقَبَةٍ مُّؤْمِنَةٍ وَدِيَةٌ مُّسَلَّمَةٌ إِلَىٰ أَهْلِهِ إِلاَّ أَن يَصَّدَّقُواْ﴾.
Severity was imposed in accidental killing only so that people would be careful about killing.
The meaning is: unless they remit the blood-money to you as charity.
It is narrated from Ubayy ibn Kaʿb that he read: ﴿إِلاَّ أَنْ يَتَصَدَّقُوْا﴾.
Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī read: ﴿إِلاَّ أَنْ تَصَّدَّقُوْا﴾.
The meaning is: إلا أن تتصدّقوا, then the تاء was assimilated into the صاد.
On this reading it is also permissible: إلا أن تَصَدَّقوا, with one of the two تاء's omitted.
His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿فَإِن كَانَ مِن قَوْمٍ عَدُوٍّ لَّكُمْ وَهُوَ مُؤْمِنٌ فَتَحْرِيرُ رَقَبَةٍ مُّؤْمِنَةٍ﴾.
The meaning of ﴿عَدُوٍّ﴾ is like the meaning of أعداء (enemies).
ʿIkrima narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās that the meaning is: if he was a believer and his people were unbelievers, then do not pay them the blood-money; and upon you is the freeing of a slave.
The meaning of this is: when a Muslim is killed by mistake and he has no Muslim people, there is no blood-money due from his killer, whether he was killed in the land of the Muslims or in the land of war.
ʿAṭāʾ ibn al-Sāʾib narrated from Abū ʿIyāḍ, who said: a man would come and accept Islam, then go to his people, who were polytheists, and stay with them; then they would flee, and he would be killed among those who were killed. So there was revealed: ﴿فَإِن كَانَ مِن قَوْمٍ عَدُوٍّ لَّكُمْ وَهُوَ مُؤْمِنٌ فَتَحْرِيرُ رَقَبَةٍ مُّؤْمِنَةٍ﴾. He said: and there is no blood-money for him.
The meaning of this is that he is killed in the land of war specifically.
Some people said: and if he is killed in the land of Islam, his ruling is the ruling of the Muslims.
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿وَإِن كَانَ مِن قَوْمٍ بَيْنَكُمْ وَبَيْنَهُمْ مِّيثَاقٌ فَدِيَةٌ مُّسَلَّمَةٌ إِلَىۤ أَهْلِهِ وَتَحْرِيرُ رَقَبَةٍ مُّؤْمِنَةٍ﴾.
Al-Zuhrī said: الميثاق is the covenant.
So the meaning is: if the one killed was from a people between whom and you there is a covenant, then pay them the blood-money, lest you inflame their breasts with rancour.
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿فَمَن لَّمْ يَجِدْ فَصِيَامُ شَهْرَيْنِ مُتَتَابِعَيْنِ﴾.
That is: whoever does not find the blood-money and the freeing of a slave, upon him is this.
﴿تَوْبَةً مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ﴾:
that is, He did this so that they might repent with a repentance.

nahhas-meani:93-93.t:
His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَمَن يَقْتُلْ مُؤْمِناً مُّتَعَمِّداً فَجَزَآؤُهُ جَهَنَّمُ خَالِداً فِيهَا﴾.
Shuʿba narrated from Manṣūr, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, who said: "Ibn Abzā told me to [ask] Ibn ʿAbbās about this verse ﴿وَمَن يَقْتُلْ مُؤْمِناً مُّتَعَمِّداً﴾. So I asked him, and he said: nothing has abrogated it."
It is narrated from Zayd ibn Thābit: the severe [verse] was revealed six months after the lenient one — ﴿وَمَن يَقْتُلْ مُؤْمِناً مُّتَعَمِّداً فَجَزَآؤُهُ جَهَنَّمُ﴾ after the one in al-Furqān ﴿وَالَّذِينَ لاَ يَدْعُوْنَ مَعَ اللَّهِ إلهَاً آخَرَ﴾ up to His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿إِلاَّ مَنْ تَابَ﴾.
Some people held that it is on the basis of requital — if He requites him with that — and that pardon may be hoped for him with repentance.
