There is no need to say «if He requites him» regarding this; rather the view on it among the scholars — the people of reasoning — is that it is decisive (muḥkam), and that He requites him if he does not repent; and if he repents, He has made his case clear by His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَإِنِّي لَغَفَّارٌ لِمَنْ تَابَ﴾; nothing is excluded from this.

nahhas-meani:94-94.t:
His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ إِذَا ضَرَبْتُمْ فِي سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ فَتَبَيَّنُواْ﴾.
It is also read: ﴿فَتَثَبَّتُوْا﴾.
Abū ʿUbayd said: each of the two is close to the other.
Someone else said: one may make sure (يُتثبَّت) without things becoming clear (يُتبيَّن), so the preferred reading is «فتبيّنوا».
The meaning of ﴿ضَرَبْتُمْ﴾ is: you travelled.
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿وَلاَ تَقُولُواْ لِمَنْ أَلْقَىۤ إِلَيْكُمُ السَّلَمَ لَسْتَ مُؤْمِناً﴾.
Ibn ʿAbbās read: ﴿لِمَنْ أَلْقَى إِلَيْكُمُ السَّلاَمَ﴾.
Whoever reads ﴿السَّلَمَ﴾, its meaning for him is submission and surrender.
Whoever reads ﴿السَّلاَمَ﴾, his reading bears two meanings:
One of them: that it is in the sense of السِّلْم (peace).
The other: that it is from the greeting (التسليم).
ʿAṭāʾ and ʿIkrima narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās "that some of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ passed by a shepherd, who said: peace be upon you. They said: he is only seeking refuge by it; so they killed him and brought his sheep to the Prophet ﷺ. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿وَلاَ تَقُولُواْ لِمَنْ أَلْقَىۤ إِلَيْكُمُ ٱلسَّلاَمَ لَسْتَ مُؤْمِناً تَبْتَغُونَ عَرَضَ ٱلْحَيَاةِ ٱلدُّنْيَا﴾."
Ibn ʿAbbās said: He means the booty.
It is narrated from Abū Jaʿfar that he read: ﴿مُؤْمَناً﴾ with fatḥa on the second mīm, from «أمنتُه» when you grant him protection, so he is مُؤْمَن (one granted safety).
* His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿كَذٰلِكَ كُنْتُمْ مِّن قَبْلُ فَمَنَّ ٱللَّهُ عَلَيْكُمْ﴾.
Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said: that is, ﴿كَذٰلِكَ كُنْتُمْ﴾ concealing your faith, ﴿فَمَنَّ ٱللَّهُ عَلَيْكُمْ﴾, that is, Allah favoured you with campaigning and making the religion manifest.
Abū ʿUbayd "al-Qāsim ibn Sallām" chose ﴿وَلاَ تَقُولُواْ لِمَنْ أَلْقَىۤ إِلَيْكُمُ ٱلسَّلاَمَ﴾.
The people of reasoning differed from him and said: (السَّلَم) is more fitting here, because it is in the sense of submission and surrender, as He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿فألقوا السَّلَمَ مَا كُنَّا نَعْمَلُ مِنْ سُوْءٍ﴾.

nahhas-meani:95-95.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿لاَّ يَسْتَوِي ٱلْقَاعِدُونَ مِنَ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾.
Ibn ʿAbbās said: those who stayed behind from Badr and those who went out to it are not equal.
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿غَيْرُ أُوْلِي ٱلضَّرَرِ﴾.
الضرر is chronic disability.
(غير) is read in the nominative and in the accusative.
Abū Isḥāq said: the genitive is also permissible.
Whoever reads the nominative, the meaning is (لاَ يَسْتَوِي الْقَاعِدُونَ غَيْرُ أُولِي الضَّرَرِ),
that is: the ones staying behind who are other than those with disability are not equal.
The meaning: the healthy ones staying behind are not equal.
Whoever reads (غَيْرَ) in the accusative, it bears two meanings:
One of them: exception, and the meaning is: except those with disability, for they are equal to those who strive.
The other meaning: that (غير) is in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial), that is: those staying behind, being healthy, are not equal.
The meaning is according to the accusative, because Zayd ibn Thābit and al-Barāʾ ibn ʿĀzib narrated that when ﴿لاَّ يَسْتَوِي ٱلْقَاعِدُونَ مِنَ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ was revealed to the Prophet ﷺ, Ibn Umm Maktūm stood and said: O Messenger of Allah, I am blind. So ﴿غَيْرُ أُوْلِي ٱلضَّرَرِ﴾ was revealed and attached to it. This is the sense of the ḥadīth.
Whoever reads the genitive, the meaning for him is: of the believers who are other than those with disability, that is, of the healthy believers.
* His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَكُـلاًّ وَعَدَ ٱللَّهُ ٱلْحُسْنَىٰ﴾.
That is, to those who strive and to those with disability Allah has promised the best.
The exegetes said: by الحسنى He means Paradise.
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿وَفَضَّلَ ٱللَّهُ ٱلْمُجَاهِدِينَ عَلَى ٱلْقَاعِدِينَ﴾ — those who have no disability — ﴿أَجْراً عَظِيْماً. دَرَجَاتٍ مِنْهُ﴾.
It is narrated from Ibn Muḥayrīz that he said: "Those are seventy degrees; between each two degrees is the gallop of the swift, lean-trained horse for seventy years."

nahhas-meani:97-97.t:
His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ تَوَفَّاهُمُ ٱلْمَلاۤئِكَةُ ظَالِمِيۤ أَنْفُسِهِمْ﴾.
ʿĪsā — he is Ibn ʿUmar — read: ﴿إنِّ الَّذِينَ يَتَوَفَّاهُمُ المَلائِكَةُ﴾. «[Translator's note: «إنِّ» is as printed in the source.]»
This is on the basis of treating the plural as masculine.
Whoever reads ﴿تَوَفَّاهُم﴾, it bears two meanings:
One of them: that it is a past verb, and it is also on the basis of treating the plural as masculine.
The other: that it is imperfect, on the basis of treating the group as feminine;
the meaning is تتوفّاهم, then one of the two تاء's was omitted.
ʿIkrima and al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: these were people who professed Islam, then did not emigrate, and went out to Badr with the polytheists and were killed. So Allah, Majestic and Mighty, revealed concerning them: ﴿إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ تَوَفَّاهُمُ ٱلْمَلاۤئِكَةُ ظَالِمِيۤ أَنْفُسِهِمْ [قَالُواْ فِيمَ كُنتُمْ﴾ — were you among the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ, or were you polytheists? This is a question of rebuke]. «[Translator's note: the source reads «ثم لم يهاجروا إلى بدر مع المشركين», literally «then did not emigrate to Badr with the polytheists»; the words «and went out» are supplied from the evident sense.]»

nahhas-meani:98-98.t:
Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿إِلاَّ ٱلْمُسْتَضْعَفِينَ مِنَ ٱلرِّجَالِ وَٱلنِّسَآءِ وَٱلْوِلْدَانِ﴾.
Mujāhid said: these were people who accepted Islam and remained firm in Islam, but had no means of emigrating, so Allah excused them and said: ﴿فَأُولئِكَ عَسَى اللَّهُ أَنْ يَعْفُوَ عَنْهُمْ﴾.
عسى expresses hope, and when Allah, Majestic and Mighty, commands that something be hoped for, it is binding; such is the right opinion of Him.

nahhas-meani:100-100.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمَن يُهَاجِرْ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ يَجِدْ فِي ٱلأَرْضِ مُرَاغَماً كَثِيراً وَسَعَةً﴾.
المراغَم and المهاجَر are one according to the linguists. One says «راغمتُ فلاناً» when you abandon him and show him enmity, as though you do not care about him even if his nose cleaves to الرَّغام, which is dust.
And it is said: it is called مهاجَر and مراغَم only because when a man accepted Islam he would show enmity to his people and abandon them; so his departure was called مراغَم, and his going to the Prophet ﷺ was called hijra.
Muʿāwiya ibn Ṣāliḥ narrated from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥa, from Ibn ʿAbbās: ﴿مُرَاغَماً﴾, he says: a moving from land to land. He said: ﴿وَسَعَةً﴾, he says: in provision.
Qatāda said: from error to guidance, that is, ampleness from the constriction he was in, in that he was unable to manifest his religion.
The word bears both meanings, because there is no specification in it.
* His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَمَن يَخْرُجْ مِن بَيْتِهِ مُهَاجِراً إِلَى ٱللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ ثُمَّ يُدْرِكْهُ ٱلْمَوْتُ فَقَدْ وَقَعَ أَجْرُهُ عَلىَ ٱللَّهِ﴾.
Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said: it was revealed concerning a man called "Ḍamra" of Khuzāʿa, who was afflicted in his sight. He said: take me out. When they reached al-Tanʿīm with him, he died, and this verse was revealed concerning him.

nahhas-meani:101-101.t:
His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَإِذَا ضَرَبْتُمْ فِي ٱلأَرْضِ فَلَيْسَ عَلَيْكُمْ جُنَاحٌ أَن تَقْصُرُواْ مِنَ ٱلصَّلاَةِ﴾.
Yaʿlā ibn Umayya said: I asked ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, may Allah be pleased with him, saying: this was only at a time of fear, and that has passed. He said: I wondered at what you wonder at, so I asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he said: "It is a charity Allah has bestowed upon you, so accept His charity."
The meaning of ﴿ضَرَبْتُمْ فِي ٱلأَرْضِ﴾ is: you travelled, as He said:
﴿وَآخَرُونَ يَضْرِبُونَ فِي الأَرْضِ يَبْتَغُونَ مِنْ فَضْلِ اللَّهِ﴾.
On the meaning of His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿فَلَيْسَ عَلَيْكُمْ جُنَاحٌ أَن تَقْصُرُواْ مِنَ ٱلصَّلاَةِ﴾ there are two views:
One of them: that it is a permission, not an obligation, as He said: ﴿فَلاَ جُنَاحَ عَلَيْهِمَا أَنْ يَتَرَاجَعَا﴾.
The other view: that this is the obligatory duty of the traveller, as ʿĀʾisha narrated: "The prayer was prescribed as two rakʿas; it was kept [so in travel, and added to in] the prayer of residence." It is then like His saying: ﴿فَلاَ جُنَاحَ عَليْهِ أَنْ يَطَّوَّفَ بِهِمَا﴾, and the circuit is obligatory.
It is narrated from Ubayy ibn Kaʿb that he read: ﴿فَلَيْسَ عَلَيْكُمْ جُنَاحٌ أَنْ تَقْصُرُوا مِنَ الصَّلاَةِ أَن يَفْتِنَكُمُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا﴾, without ﴿إِنْ خِفْتُمْ﴾ in it.
So the meaning according to his reading is: out of aversion that those who disbelieve should afflict you; then the word was omitted, like (وَاسْأَلِ الْقَرْيَةَ).
One says: قَصَرَ الصلاة, قَصَّرها and أقصرها.
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿إِنَّ ٱلْكَافِرِينَ كَانُواْ لَكُمْ عَدُوّاً مُّبِيناً﴾.
عدوّ here is in the sense of أعداء (enemies).

nahhas-meani:102-102.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَإِذَا كُنتَ فِيهِمْ فَأَقَمْتَ لَهُمُ ٱلصَّلاَةَ﴾.
Sufyān narrated from Manṣūr, from Mujāhid, from Abū ʿAyyāsh al-Zuraqī, who said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed at ʿUsfān, with the polytheists between him and the fighting; among them — or over them — was Khālid ibn al-Walīd. The polytheists said: they were in a prayer; had we struck at them, there would have been booty. Then the polytheists said: there will come a prayer that is dearer to them than their fathers and their sons. He said: and Jibrīl came down with the verses between the ẓuhr and the ʿaṣr." And he mentioned the ḥadīth.
We shall mention the ḥadīth of "Ṣāliḥ ibn Khawwāt" which the people of Medina follow; we disliked being lengthy about that.
In the ḥadīth of Ṣāliḥ, each group completes its prayer before turning away from the qibla, and the others are not like that.
The meaning is: when you are among them and there is fear.
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿فَلْتَقُمْ طَآئِفَةٌ مِّنْهُمْ مَّعَكَ وَلْيَأْخُذُوۤاْ أَسْلِحَتَهُمْ﴾.
The meaning is: and let the rest take their weapons.
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿فَإِذَا سَجَدُواْ فَلْيَكُونُواْ مِن وَرَآئِكُمْ﴾.
The people of Medina follow, regarding the prayer of fear, the ḥadīth of Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd al-Anṣārī, from al-Qāsim ibn Muḥammad, from Ṣāliḥ ibn Khawwāt al-Anṣārī, that Sahl ibn Abī Ḥathma told him that the prayer of fear is that the imam stands facing the qibla with a group of his companions, while a group faces the enemy. The imam bows one rakʿa and prostrates with those who are with him, then stands; when he is upright standing he remains so, and [they complete] the second rakʿa by themselves, then give the salām and leave while the imam is standing, and they take position facing the enemy. Then the others, who have not prayed, come forward and say the takbīr with the imam; he bows one rakʿa with them and prostrates, then gives the salām; and they stand and bow the remaining rakʿa by themselves, then give the salām.
His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَلْيَأْخُذُواْ حِذْرَهُمْ وَأَسْلِحَتَهُمْ﴾.
It is possible that this is for all of them, because even though those in the prayer are not fighting, if they have their weapons with them that is more awe-inspiring to the enemy.
And it is possible that those commanded to take weapons are those who are not in the prayer, because the one praying does not fight.

nahhas-meani:103-103.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَإِذَا قَضَيْتُمُ ٱلصَّلاَةَ فَٱذْكُرُواْ ٱللَّهَ قِيَاماً وَقُعُوداً وَعَلَىٰ جُنُوبِكُمْ﴾.
That is: remember Him with thanks, glorification, and whatever brings one near to Him.
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿فَإِذَا ٱطْمَأْنَنتُمْ﴾.
Mujāhid said: when you are among your families and homes.
What is known in the language is that one says اطمأنّ when he becomes still; so the meaning is: when fear has subsided from you and you have reached your dwellings, ﴿فَأَقِيمُواْ ٱلصَّلاَةَ﴾.
Mujāhid said: that is, complete it.
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿إِنَّ ٱلصَّلاَةَ كَانَتْ عَلَى ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ كِتَاباً مَّوْقُوتاً﴾.
Layth narrated from Mujāhid that الموقوت is the prescribed.
Ibn Abī Najīḥ narrated from Mujāhid that he said: (مَوْقُوتَاً) means obligatory.
Zayd ibn Aslam said: (موقوتاً) means divided into fixed instalments (مُنَجَّم), that is, you perform it at its appointed times.
The meaning according to the linguists is: prescribed for a specific time. One says: [وَقَّتَهُ فهو مَوْقُوْتٌ] and وَقَّتَهُ فهو مُوَقَّت. This is exactly the view of Zayd ibn Aslam. «[Translator's note: the expected form here is «وَقَتَهُ» without doubling, which yields موقوت; the source has «وَقَّتَهُ».]»

nahhas-meani:11-11.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يُوصِيكُمُ ٱللَّهُ فِيۤ أَوْلاَدِكُمْ﴾.
That is: He makes it obligatory upon you, as He said: ﴿وَلاْ تَقْتُلُوْا النَّفْسَ الَّتِي حَرَّمَ اللَّهُ إِلاَّ بِالْحَقِّ، ذَلِكُمْ وَصَّاكُمْ بِهِ﴾.
* Then He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿لِلذَّكَرِ مِثْلُ حَظِّ ٱلأُنْثَيَيْنِ﴾.
In opposition to the people of the Jāhiliyya, because they used not to let females inherit.
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَإِن كُنَّ نِسَآءً فَوْقَ ٱثْنَتَيْنِ فَلَهُنَّ ثُلُثَا مَا تَرَكَ﴾.
He did not specify anything for two [daughters], and there are several views on this:
a - Among them is that it has been said: "فوق" here is redundant (zāʾida), and the meaning is: if they are women, two [in number], as He said: ﴿فَاضْرِبُوْا فَوْقَ اْلأعْنَاقِ﴾.
b - And it has been said: the two were given two-thirds by inference, not by explicit text.
Because Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, made these things point to one another, so that the Muslims would gain understanding of them.
The proof: that He made the share of the uterine sisters and brothers one and the same when they are two or more; He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَإِنْ كَاْنَ رَجُلٌ يُوْرَثُ كَلاَلَةً أَو امْرَأَةٌ وَلَهُ أَخٌ أَوْ أُخْتٌ فَلِكُلِّ وَاحِدٍ مِنْهُمَا السُّدُسُ فَإِنْ كَانُوا أَكْثَرَ مِنْ ذَلِكَ فَهُمْ شُرَكَاءُ فِيْ الثُلُثِ﴾.
c - Another proof: that He made the share of the sister like the share of the daughter; therefore the share of two daughters must be like the share of two sisters.
Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿يَسْتَفْتُوْنَكَ، قُل اللَّهُ يُفْتِيْكُمْ فِي الْكَلاَلَةِ، إِنِ امْرُوٌ هَلَكَ لَيْسَ لَهُ وَلَدٌ، وَلَهُ أُخْتٌ فَلَهَا نِصْفُ مَا تَرَكَ﴾.
Abū al-ʿAbbās "Muḥammad ibn Yazīd" said: In the verse itself there is proof that two daughters get two-thirds, because He said ﴿لِلذَّكَرِ مِثْلُ حَظِّ ٱلأُنْثَيَيْنِ﴾, and the least number is a male and a female; so if the single [female] gets a third, that shows that two [females] get two-thirds. These are the views of the linguists.
It has also been said: daughters get only a half or two-thirds; so since it was necessary that two daughters not have [Translator's note: a word appears to be missing here, presumably "the half"], it was necessary that they have two-thirds.
This, even though Ibn ʿAbbās said: They get a half.
And it is soundly established from the Prophet ﷺ that he gave two daughters two-thirds.
Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh related that the wife of "Saʿd ibn al-Rabīʿ" came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: O Messenger of Allah, my husband was killed with you, and women are only married for wealth; he has left me, and left two daughters and a brother, and the brother has taken the wealth. So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ summoned him and said: "Give her the eighth, and the two daughters two-thirds, and what remains is yours."
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَإِن كَانَ لَهُ إِخْوَةٌ فَلأُمِّهِ ٱلسُّدُسُ﴾.
The jurists are agreed that "brothers" means two or more, except Ibn ʿAbbās, for he said: "Brothers" are not fewer than three.
The proof that two are called "brothers" is His saying ﴿وَإِنْ كَانُوا إِخْوَةً رِجَالاً وَنِسَاءً﴾; there is no disagreement among the people of knowledge that this applies to two or more. And two are a group, because it is one that you have joined to another.
And He said ﴿وَأَطْرَافَ النَّهَارِ﴾, meaning its two ends — and Allah knows best.
And the prayer of two is a congregation.
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿مِن بَعْدِ وَصِيَّةٍ يُوصِي بِهَآ أَوْ دَيْنٍ﴾.
It is related from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: You recite ﴿مِن بَعْدِ وَصِيَّةٍ يُوصِي بِهَآ أَوْ دَيْنٍ﴾, yet the Messenger of Allah ﷺ ruled that the debt comes before the bequest.
Abū Jaʿfar said: It is as though this is by way of advancing and postponing (taqdīm wa-taʾkhīr); and "أوْ" here is not in the sense of "و" (and), but is only for permission (ibāḥa).
The difference between it and "و" is that, had He said "مِنْ بَعْدِ وَصِيَّةٍ يُوْصِي بِهَا وَدَيْنٍ", the hearer might imagine that this [applies] when both are combined; but when He brought "أَوْ", it allows that they be combined, and that there be only one of them.
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿آبَآؤُكُمْ وَأَبناؤُكُمْ لاَ تَدْرُونَ أَيُّهُمْ أَقْرَبُ لَكُمْ نَفْعاً﴾.
Ibn ʿAbbās said: In this world.
Someone else said: If the son is of a higher degree than the father, he asks Allah to join him to himself; and likewise the father, if he is of a higher degree than him.
* Then He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿فَرِيضَةً مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ كَانَ عَلِيماً حَكِيماً﴾.
That is: All-Knowing of what He made obligatory, All-Wise in it.
There are several views on the meaning of ﴿كَاْنَ﴾ here:
One of them [Translator's note: the text has "أحدهما" (one of two)]: that its meaning is "has never ceased to be"; as though the people had witnessed wisdom and knowledge, so Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, informed them that He has never ceased to be so.
It has also been said: Allah's informing about the past and the future is one and the same, because it is known to Him.

nahhas-meani:12-12.t:
And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿وَإِن كَانَ رَجُلٌ يُورَثُ كَلاَلَةً أَو ٱمْرَأَةٌ﴾.
There are several views on «الكلالة»:
The Basrans said: «الكلالة» is the deceased who has neither child nor parent.
They adduced as proof that it is related — with a disagreement [in the report] — from Abū Bakr, and from ʿAlī, Zayd ibn Thābit, Ibn Masʿūd, Ibn ʿAbbās and Jābir ibn Zayd, that they said: «الكلالة» is one who has neither child nor parent.
The Basrans said: This is like your saying "a barren man", when no child is born [to him]. It is derived from al-iklīl (the crown/wreath), as though the heirs had surrounded him while he has neither child nor parent, so they take possession of the wealth.
The people of Medina and the people of Kufa said: «الكلالة» is the heirs among whom there is neither parent nor child.
Two views are related from ʿUmar:
One of them: that «الكلالة» is one who has neither child nor parent.
And the other: that it is one who has no child.
Abū Jaʿfar said: An anomalous (shādhdh) view is related from ʿAṭāʾ; he said: «الكلالة» is the wealth.
Ibn Zayd said: «الكلالة» is the deceased who has neither parent nor child, and the living are all «كلالة»; this one inherits by «كلالة» and this one is inherited from by «كلالة».
Muḥammad ibn Jarīr said: The correct view is that «الكلالة» are those who inherit from the deceased other than his child and his parent, because of the soundness of the report of Jābir — meaning Ibn ʿAbd Allāh — that he said: I said: O Messenger of Allah, only «كلالة» will inherit from me, so how is the inheritance? And [the verse] was revealed.
* Then He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿وَلَهُ أَخٌ أَوْ أُخْتٌ فَلِكُلِّ وَاحِدٍ مِّنْهُمَا ٱلسُّدُسُ﴾.
He means here only the uterine brothers and sisters.
Likewise it is related from Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ that he read: ﴿وَلَهُ أَحٌ أُوْ أُخْتٌ "مِن أُمِّهِ" فَلِكُلِّ وَاحِدٍ مِنْهُمَا السُّدُسُ﴾.
Al-Ḥasan and Abū Rajāʾ read: ﴿يُوْرِثُ كلالةً﴾.
Hārūn the Reader said: Some of the people of Kufa read: ﴿يُوَرِّثُ كلالةً﴾.
So according to these two readings «الكلالة» can only be the heirs or the wealth.
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿مِن بَعْدِ وَصِيَّةٍ يُوصَىٰ بِهَآ أَوْ دَيْنٍ غَيْرَ مُضَآرٍّ﴾.
It is related from al-Ḥasan that he read: ﴿غَيْرَ مُضَارِّ وَصِيَةٍ مِنَ اللَّهِ﴾, as a genitive construct (muḍāf). Some linguists have claimed that this is a grammatical error (laḥn), because the active participle is not put in construct with the maṣdar (verbal noun).
But the reading is good on the basis of an omission; the meaning is: not harming the possessor of a bequest, i.e. not harming his heirs by it in their inheritance.

nahhas-meani:13-13.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿تِلْكَ حُدُودُ ٱللَّهِ﴾.
That is: what He has forbidden to be overstepped. And ḥadadtu means: I prevented.
* Then He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿وَمَن يُطِعِ ٱللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ يُدْخِلْهُ جَنَّاتٍ تَجْرِي مِن تَحْتِهَا ٱلأَنْهَارُ﴾.
That is: whoever obeys Him in what He has made obligatory and set as a limit.

nahhas-meani:14-14.t:
Then He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿وَمَن يَعْصِ ٱللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ وَيَتَعَدَّ حُدُودَهُ يُدْخِلْهُ نَاراً﴾.
The meaning of "يتعدَّى" is: he oversteps, i.e. he oversteps what has been set as a limit for him.

nahhas-meani:15-15.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَٱللاَّتِي يَأْتِينَ ٱلْفَاحِشَةَ مِن نِّسَآئِكُمْ فَٱسْتَشْهِدُواْ عَلَيْهِنَّ أَرْبَعةً مِّنْكُمْ فَإِن شَهِدُواْ فَأَمْسِكُوهُنَّ فِي ٱلْبُيُوتِ﴾.
This verse is abrogated.
Ibn ʿAbbās said: The matter was so until the verse was revealed: ﴿الزَّانِيَةُ وَالزَّانِي فَاجْلِدُوْا كُلَّ وَاحِدٍ مِنْهُمَا مِائَةَ جَلْدَةٍ﴾.
As for the meaning of the abrogated verse, Sufyān and al-Suddī said: "When a previously married person (thayyib) committed fornication, he was confined until he died; and when an unmarried person committed fornication, he was reviled verbally."
Except that the benefit [remaining] in the verse is that nothing fewer than four [witnesses] was accepted in cases of fornication.
Mujāhid claimed regarding His saying ﴿وَٱللاَّتِي يَأْتِينَ ٱلْفَاحِشَةَ مِن نِّسَآئِكُمْ﴾ that it was specific to women, not men, and that the one after it is specific to men, namely ﴿وَالَّلذَانِ يَأْتِيَانِهَا مِنْكُمْ فَآذُوْهُمَا﴾ — with reviling; then both were abrogated by the prescribed ḥadd punishment. This is the meaning of what he said.
Abū Jaʿfar said: This is what is correct in the language, being the literal sense; the masculine is not given precedence over the feminine except with proof.
As for the meaning of ﴿أَوْ يَجْعَلَ ٱللَّهُ لَهُنَّ سَبِيلاً﴾, ʿUbāda ibn al-Ṣāmit related that the Prophet ﷺ said: "Take from me: Allah has made a way for them. The unmarried with the unmarried: a hundred lashes and banishment for a year; the previously married with the previously married: a hundred lashes and stoning."
It has been said: this ḥadīth is abrogated, namely [in] that the previously married person is not flogged but only stoned. This ḥadīth was abrogated by the ḥadīth of al-Zuhrī, from ʿUbayd Allāh [ibn ʿAbd Allāh], from Abū Hurayra and Zayd ibn Khālid: "A man came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: O Messenger of Allah, my son was a hired worker for this man, and he committed adultery with his wife. I ransomed him from him, then I was told that my son is liable to a hundred lashes and banishment for a year, and his wife to stoning. So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ ruled that what had been taken from him be returned to him, that his son be given a hundred lashes and banished for a year, and that the woman be stoned; and he did not order her to be flogged."
It is also said: the ḥadīth of ʿUbāda was at the beginning, and banishment is not obligatory unless the ruler sees fit, since it is possible that the banishment on his part ﷺ was because of something he knew about the one being flogged.
The saying of [ʿAlī] ibn Abī Ṭālib, may Allah be pleased with him, that the previously married person is liable to both flogging and stoning, is the view of the people of reasoned investigation, because the abrogation of flogging along with stoning has not been made clear; so the flogging stands firm, and there is more than one proof for it.

nahhas-meani:17-17.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِنَّمَا ٱلتَّوْبَةُ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ لِلَّذِينَ يَعْمَلُونَ ٱلسُّوۤءَ بِجَهَالَةٍ﴾.
Qatāda said: The Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ gathered and were of the view that everyone who disobeys Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, is ignorant.
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ثُمَّ يَتُوبُونَ مِن قَرِيبٍ﴾.
It is related from al-Ḍaḥḥāk that he said: Everything short of death is "near".

nahhas-meani:18-18.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلَيْسَتِ ٱلتَّوْبَةُ لِلَّذِينَ يَعْمَلُونَ ٱلسَّيِّئَاتِ حَتَّىٰ إِذَا حَضَرَ أَحَدَهُمُ ٱلْمَوْتُ قَالَ إِنِّي تُبْتُ ٱلآنَ﴾.
It is related from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar that he said: The presence of death is nothing but the death-throes (al-sawq); meaning that when he sees [it] with his own eyes, the truth becomes clear to him, and repentance does not benefit him at that point, as He, Majestic and Mighty is He, said of Pharaoh: ﴿آمنتُ﴾.

nahhas-meani:19-19.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ لاَ يَحِلُّ لَكُمْ أَن تَرِثُواْ ٱلنِّسَآءَ كَرْهاً﴾.
Al-Zuhrī and Abū Mijlaz said: This was in a clan of the Anṣār. When a man died and left a wife, his next of kin would throw a cloak over her, and she would then be unable to marry. This is the gist of what the two of them said. Others added: and he would marry her without a dower, and perhaps he would harass her, and she could not marry until she ransomed herself from him. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, revealed ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ لاَ يَحِلُّ لَكُمْ أَن تَرِثُواْ ٱلنِّسَآءَ كَرْهاً﴾ — the verse.
So the meaning would be: it is not lawful for you to inherit them from their husbands and so become husbands to them.
It is also possible that the meaning is: do not marry them in order to inherit from them against their will, so that the inheritance comes about from them while they are averse to the contract that makes inheritance due.
It is also read ﴿كُرْهَاً﴾.
Al-Farrāʾ holds that the meaning of ﴿كَرْهَاً﴾ is that you are compelled to do something, while al-kurh, coming from oneself, he takes to be in the sense of hardship.
Al-Kisāʾī said: al-karh and al-kurh are one and the same.
And according to the Basrans it is as al-Kisāʾī said; they are two dialectal variants.
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلاَ تَعْضُلُوهُنَّ ُلِتَذْهَبُواْ بِبَعْضِ مَآ آتَيْتُمُوهُنَّ﴾.
Mujāhid said: It is like the one in [Sūrat] al-Baqara.
He holds that its meaning is: and do not detain them.
It is related that a man would marry a woman and she would not please him, so he would detain her and harass her until she ransomed herself from him.
Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿إِلاَّ أَن يَأْتِينَ بِفَاحِشَةٍ مُّبَيِّنَةٍ﴾.
Al-Ḥasan and al-Shaʿbī said: He means fornication.
Al-Shaʿbī said: If she does that, khulʿ (divorce for compensation) becomes valid, and he may demand it from her.
Miqsam said: This is when she disobeys you and harms you.
ʿAṭāʾ al-Khurāsānī said: When a man married a woman and she committed an indecency, he could take back from her everything he had given her. Then that was abrogated by the ḥadd punishments.
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَعَاشِرُوهُنَّ بِٱلْمَعْرُوفِ﴾.
That is: in spending the night, maintenance and speech.

nahhas-meani:20-20.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَإِنْ أَرَدْتُّمُ ٱسْتِبْدَالَ زَوْجٍ مَّكَانَ زَوْجٍ﴾.
That is: divorcing and marrying.
Then He said: ﴿وَآتَيْتُمْ إِحْدَاهُنَّ قِنْطَاراً﴾. Al-qinṭār is a great amount of wealth, and we have mentioned it in Sūrat Āl ʿImrān.
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أَتَأْخُذُونَهُ بُهْتَاناً وَإِثْماً مُّبِيناً﴾? [verse 20].
Al-buhtān in the language is: falsehood whose falseness leaves one bewildered; and from it: buhita the man, when he was bewildered.

nahhas-meani:104-104.t:
His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَلاَ تَهِنُواْ فِي ٱبْتِغَآءِ ٱلْقَوْمِ﴾.
That is: do not weaken. One says: وَهَنَ يَهِنُ وَهْناً ووُهُوناً.
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿إِن تَكُونُواْ تَأْلَمُونَ فَإِنَّهُمْ يَأْلَمُونَ كَمَا تَأْلَمونَ﴾.
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: that is, you are in pain.
﴿وَتَرْجُونَ مِنَ ٱللَّهِ مَا لاَ يَرْجُونَ﴾.
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: that is, in your wounds; he means: of reward.
Someone else said: you hope for victory and well-being that they do not hope for.
And it is said: ﴿تَرْجُونَ﴾ means: you fear.

nahhas-meani:105-105.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِنَّآ أَنْزَلْنَا إِلَيْكَ ٱلْكِتَابَ بِٱلْحَقِّ لِتَحْكُمَ بَيْنَ ٱلنَّاسِ بِمَآ أَرَاكَ ٱللَّهُ وَلاَ تَكُنْ لِّلْخَآئِنِينَ خَصِيماً﴾.
Mujāhid said: there was a man of the Anṣār called "Ibn Ubayriq", whose name was "Ṭuʿma"; he stole a coat of mail, and when he was suspected he deposited it with a man of the Jews and claimed that the Jew had taken it. His people came asking the Prophet ﷺ to clear him, so Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿إِنَّآ أَنْزَلْنَا إِلَيْكَ ٱلْكِتَابَ بِٱلْحَقِّ﴾ up to His saying: ﴿وَلاَ تُجَادِل عَنِ الَّذِينَ يَخْتَانُونَ أَنْفُسَهُمْ﴾.
الجدال in the language is the most intense disputation. One says «a man who is أجدل» when he is strong, and the falcon is called أجدل because it is among the strongest of birds.

nahhas-meani:108-108.t:
Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿يَسْتَخْفُونَ مِنَ ٱلنَّاسِ وَلاَ يَسْتَخْفُونَ مِنَ ٱللَّهِ وَهُوَ مَعَهُمْ إِذْ يُبَيِّتُونَ مَا لاَ يَرْضَىٰ مِنَ ٱلْقَوْلِ﴾.
That is: they settle it by night.

nahhas-meani:109-109.t:
His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿هَا أَنْتُمْ هَـٰؤُلاۤءِ جَادَلْتُمْ عَنْهُمْ فِي ٱلْحَيَاةِ ٱلدُّنْيَا فَمَن يُجَادِلُ ٱللَّهَ عَنْهُمْ يَوْمَ ٱلْقِيَامَةِ﴾? [verse 109].
That is: on the day when realities become manifest; in this world judgement is only by what is apparent.
Abū Jaʿfar said: Abū Isḥāq said: the meaning is «ها أنتم الذين» (here you are, those who…).
He holds that «هؤلاء» is in the sense of «الذين» (a relative noun).

nahhas-meani:110-110.t:
Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿وَمَن يَعْمَلْ سُوۤءاً أَوْ يَظْلِمْ نَفْسَهُ ثُمَّ يَسْتَغْفِرِ ٱللَّهَ يَجِدِ ٱللَّهَ غَفُوراً رَّحِيماً﴾.
That is: the seeking of forgiveness of one who does not return to the sin, because if he is resolved to return he is not repentant.

nahhas-meani:111-111.t:
Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿وَمَن يَكْسِبْ إِثْماً فَإِنَّمَا يَكْسِبُهُ عَلَىٰ نَفْسِهِ﴾.
That is: its punishment comes back upon him.

nahhas-meani:112-112.t:
﴿وَمَن يَكْسِبْ خَطِيۤئَةً أَوْ إِثْماً ثُمَّ يَرْمِ بِهِ بَرِيئاً﴾.
Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said: it was revealed concerning Ibn Ubayriq, when he accused the Jew of taking the coat of mail that he had stolen.
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿فَقَدِ ٱحْتَمَلَ بُهْتَاناً وَإِثْماً مُّبِيناً﴾.
البهتان is the lie at whose enormity one is bewildered.

nahhas-meani:113-113.t:
Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿وَلَوْلاَ فَضْلُ ٱللَّهِ عَلَيْكَ وَرَحْمَتُهُ﴾.
That is: in that what Ibn Ubayriq had done was revealed to you.
﴿لَهَمَّتْ طَّآئِفَةٌ مِّنْهُمْ أَن يُضِلُّوكَ﴾:
that is, to make you err in the judgement.
﴿وَمَا يُضِلُّونَ إِلاَّ أَنْفُسَهُمْ وَمَا يَضُرُّونَكَ مِن شَيْءٍ﴾:
that is, because you are protected from error.
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿وَأَنزَلَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَيْكَ ٱلْكِتَابَ وَٱلْحِكْمَةَ﴾.
That is: He sent down to you the Book with wisdom in the matter of Ibn Ubayriq.

nahhas-meani:114-114.t:
His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿لاَّ خَيْرَ فِي كَثِيرٍ مِّن نَّجْوَاهُمْ﴾.
النجوى is any speech that a group keeps among themselves, whether secret or open.
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿إِلاَّ مَنْ أَمَرَ بِصَدَقَةٍ﴾.
It is possible that the meaning is: except the private talk of one who enjoins charity; then the muḍāf (the first term of the construct) was omitted.
And it is possible that it is an exception not of the same kind as what precedes, and the meaning is: but whoever enjoins charity in his private talk — there is good in it.

nahhas-meani:115-115.t:
His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَمَن يُشَاقِقِ ٱلرَّسُولَ﴾.
That is: opposes, as though he moves into a side (شِقّ) other than his side, that is, into another direction.
Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said: when Allah informed the Prophet of the affair of "Ibn Ubayriq", he fled to the polytheists and apostatised, so Allah revealed: ﴿وَمَن يُشَاقِقِ ٱلرَّسُولَ مِن بَعْدِ مَا تَبَيَّنَ لَهُ ٱلْهُدَىٰ وَيَتَّبِعْ غَيْرَ سَبِيلِ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ نُوَلِّهِ مَا تَوَلَّىٰ﴾.
Mujāhid said: that is, We leave him with what he worships.
So it is in the language: one says «وليّته ما تولّى» when you leave him to his own choice.
Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said: when he reached Mecca he broke into a house in Mecca, and the polytheists caught up with him and killed him; so Allah revealed: ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ لاَ يَغْفِرُ أَنْ يُشْرَكَ بِهِ﴾ up to His saying: ﴿فَقَدْ ضَلَّ ضَلاَلاً بَعِيداً﴾.

nahhas-meani:117-117.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِن يَدْعُونَ مِن دُونِهِ إِلاَّ إِنَاثاً﴾.
Mujāhid said: He means the idols.
And from Ubayy: with every idol there is a female jinn.
The linguists said: they were called «females» only because they named them "al-Lāt, al-ʿUzzā and Manāt", and these are feminine in their usage.
Al-Ḥasan said: that is, they worship nothing but stones and wood.
He said: every tribe had an idol that they worshipped, and it would be called «the female of Banū So-and-so»; so Allah revealed this.
This is a good view linguistically, because these things are spoken of with the feminine.
One says: «الحجارة يُعجبنه» (the stones please him, feminine plural), and one does not say «يُعجبونه» (masculine plural).
It is narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās that he read: ﴿إِنْ يَدْعُونَ مِنْ دُونِهِ إِلاَّ أُنُثَاً﴾. This is a plural of a plural, as though he pluralised وَثَن as وِثان, just as you say مِثال and مُثُل; then the واو was replaced by a hamza when it took ḍamma, as He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿وَإِذَا الرَّسُلُ أُقِّتَتْ﴾, from الوقت. «[Translator's note: the explanation via وثن / وثان fits the reading «أُثُناً» rather than «أُنُثاً» as printed here; the source is translated as written.]»
It has also been read: ﴿إِنْ يَدْعُونَ مِنْ دُونِهِ إِلاَّ أُنُثَاً﴾, and it is the plural of إناث.
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿وَإِن يَدْعُونَ إِلاَّ شَيْطَاناً مَّرِيداً لَّعَنَهُ ٱللَّهُ﴾.
المريد is the one [who has gone out] of good and is stripped of it; «أمرد» (beardless) is from this.
And it is said: المريد is the one extended in evil, from their saying «a مُمرَّد house», that is, made lofty.
The meaning of ﴿لَعَنَهُ﴾ is: He distanced him from His mercy.

nahhas-meani:118-118.t:
Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿وَقَالَ لأَتَّخِذَنَّ مِنْ عِبَادِكَ نَصِيباً مَّفْرُوضاً﴾.
That is: fixed; it is from فرضتُ, that is, I cut off.

nahhas-meani:119-119.t:
Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿وَلأُضِلَّنَّهُمْ وَلأُمَنِّيَنَّهُمْ﴾.
That is: and I will make them imagine that they have a share of good in disobedience.
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿وَلأَمُرَنَّهُمْ فَلَيُبَتِّكُنَّ آذَانَ ٱلأَنْعَامِ﴾.
One says بتّك when he cut.
Qatāda said: He means the baḥīra.
The baḥīra is the she-camel which, when she had borne five litters and the last of them was a male, they would slit her ears and not make use of her.
The implied construction in Arabic is: «and I will command them to slit the ears of the cattle».
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿وَلأَمُرَنَّهُمْ فَلَيُغَيِّرُنَّ خَلْقَ ٱللَّهِ﴾.
From Ibn ʿAbbās: the religion of Allah.
And also from him: castration.
The like is narrated from Anas.
Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, Mujāhid, Ibrāhīm, al-Ḍaḥḥāk and Qatāda said: He means the religion of Allah.
Mujāhid added: He means the fiṭra (innate disposition); that is, they were born upon Islam, and Satan commanded them to change it.
Two views are narrated from ʿIkrima:
One of them: that it is castration.
The other: that it is the religion of Allah.
These views are not contradictory, because they come back to deeds.
As for His saying ﴿لاَ تَبْدِيلَ لِخَلْقِ اللَّهِ﴾ while He said here ﴿فَلَيُغَيِّرُنَّ خَلْقَ ٱللَّهِ﴾: substitution (التبديل) is the nullifying of the very essence of a thing, so here it differs from alteration (التغيير).
Muḥammad ibn Jarīr said: the most fitting of them is that it is the religion of Allah. And if that is its meaning, there enters into it the doing of everything Allah has forbidden — castration, tattooing and other acts of disobedience — because Satan calls to all acts of disobedience; that is: and they will alter what Allah has created of His religion.

nahhas-meani:121-121.t:
His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿أُولئِكَ مَأْوَاهُمْ جَهَنَّمُ وَلاَ يَجِدُونَ عَنْهَا مَحِيصاً﴾.
المحيص in the language is a place of turning aside and a refuge.
One says حِصْتُ, جِضْتُ and عَدَلْتُ with one meaning.

nahhas-meani:123-123.t:
His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿لَّيْسَ بِأَمَانِيِّكُمْ وَلاۤ أَمَانِيِّ أَهْلِ ٱلْكِتَابِ﴾.
The meaning is: the reward is not according to your wishes.
[That this is] the meaning is indicated by His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿والذين آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحَاتِ سَنُدْخِلُهُمْ جَنَّاتٍ تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الأَنْهَارُ﴾.
His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿مَن يَعْمَلْ سُوۤءًا يُجْزَ بِهِ﴾.
It is narrated from Abū Hurayra that he said: "When ﴿مَن يَعْمَلْ سُوۤءًا يُجْزَ بِهِ وَلاَ يَجِدْ لَهُ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ وَلِيّاً وَلاَ نَصِيراً﴾ was revealed, we wept and grieved and said: O Messenger, this verse has left nothing. He said: By Him in whose hand is my soul, it is just as it was revealed; but rejoice, keep close to what is right, and aim straight, for no affliction befalls any of you but that Allah expiates a sin of his by it, even the thorn that pricks one of you in his foot."
ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥa narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās: ﴿مَن يَعْمَلْ سُوۤءًا يُجْزَ بِهِ﴾,
he says: "Whoever associates partners with Him — and that is the evil — unless he repents before his death, and Allah accepts his repentance."
ʿAbd al-Salām ibn Sahl al-Sukkarī narrated to us; he said: ʿUbayd Allāh narrated to us; he said: ʿAbd al-Wāḥid ibn Ziyād narrated to us; he said: ʿĀṣim narrated to us, from al-Ḥasan: ﴿مَن يَعْمَلْ سُوۤءًا يُجْزَ بِهِ﴾ — he said: that is for whomever Allah, Majestic and Mighty, wills [to humiliate]; as for whomever He wills to honour, no. Allah has mentioned a people and said: ﴿أُولئِكَ الَّذِينَ نَتَقَبَّلُ عَنْهُمْ أَحْسَنَ مَا عَملُوْا وَنَتَجَاوَزُ عَنْ سَيِّئَاتِهِمْ فِي أَصْحَابِ الْجَنَّةِ، وَعْدَ الصِّدْقِ الَّذِي كَانُوا يُوعَدُونَ﴾.
The ḥadīth from the Prophet ﷺ indicates that it is general.
Abū Hurayra narrated from him that he said, when this verse was revealed: "Everything with which the servant is afflicted is an expiation."
The wording of the verse is general for everyone who does evil, believer or unbeliever, whether the sin is small or great; and this agrees with «نُكَفِّر», because the meaning of «نكفّر» is: We cover them over on the Day of Resurrection, so We do not disgrace you by them.

nahhas-meani:124-124.t:
His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَلاَ يُظْلَمُونَ نَقِيراً﴾.
The meaning is: they will not be wronged by the measure of a نقير; النقير is the dot found in the date-stone; it is said that the palm sprouts from it.

nahhas-meani:125-125.t:
His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَٱتَّخَذَ ٱللَّهُ إِبْرَاهِيمَ خَلِيلاً﴾.
الخليل in the language has several meanings:
One of them: the poor man, as though he has a want (الاختلال) in him, as Zuhayr said:
وَإِنْ أَتَاهُ خَلِيلٌ يَومَ مَسأَلَةٍ * يَقُولُ لاَ غَائِبٌ مَالِي وَلاَ حَرِمُ
(And if a needy man comes to him on a day of asking, he says: my wealth is neither absent nor forbidden.)
And الخليل is the lover.
It is said regarding the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَٱتَّخَذَ ٱللَّهُ إِبْرَاهِيمَ خَلِيلاً﴾: that is, one in need, poor towards Him.
The other view, which the people of ḥadīth hold: that he is the lover devoted exclusively to Allah, in whose devotion there is no flaw.
The third view: that one says «so-and-so is the خليل of so-and-so», that is, he singles him out for intimacy.
From it is the ḥadīth: "If I were to take a خليل, I would take Abū Bakr as a خليل."
By this he indicated that he ﷺ did not single out anyone with any knowledge to the exclusion of others.

nahhas-meani:21-21.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَكَيْفَ تَأْخُذُونَهُ وَقَدْ أَفْضَىٰ بَعْضُكُمْ إِلَىٰ بَعْضٍ﴾? [verse 21].
Ibn ʿAbbās said: al-ifḍāʾ is: sexual intercourse.
The origin of al-ifḍāʾ in the language is: intermingling; and a mixed thing is called faḍan.
The poet said:
فَقُلْتُ لَهَا يَاعَمَّتَا لَكِ نَاقَتِي * وتَمُرٌ فَضَاً في عَيْبَتِيْ وَزَبِيْبُ
(So I said to her: O aunt, my she-camel is yours, and dates mixed loosely in my saddlebag, and raisins.)
And one says: "the people are fawḍā faḍan", i.e. mixed together, with no commander over them.
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَأَخَذْنَ مِنكُم مِّيثَاقاً غَلِيظاً﴾.
Ibn ʿAbbās and al-Ḥasan said: It is His saying: ﴿فَأَمْسِكُوْهُنَّ بِمَعْرُوْفِ أَوْ سَرَّحُوْهُنَّ بِمَعْرُوِفٍ﴾.
He made it the equivalent of a solemn covenant, i.e. an oath, figuratively (majāzan).
Mujāhid and ʿIkrima said: You made them lawful for yourselves by Allah's trust, and you took possession of them by the word of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He.

nahhas-meani:22-22.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلاَ تَنكِحُواْ مَا نَكَحَ آبَاؤُكُمْ مِّنَ ٱلنِّسَآءِ إِلاَّ مَا قَدْ سَلَفَ﴾.
It may be asked: How did He except ﴿مَا قَدْ سَلَفَ﴾ from what had not yet happened?
The answer: this is an exception not from the first [i.e. a disjoined exception], and the Arabs say: "It did not increase, except what decreased."
[Sībawayh] makes "إلاَّ" in the sense of "لكنْ" (but): the meaning is: but what has already passed is forgiven, or: so leave it.
Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿إِنَّهُ كَانَ فَاحِشَةً وَمَقْتاً وَسَآءَ سَبِيلاً﴾.
It may be asked: Why was (كان) brought, when it is an indecency in every case?
There are two answers to this:
Abū Isḥāq said: Abū al-ʿAbbās Muḥammad ibn Yazīd said:
"كان" here is redundant (zāʾida), and the meaning is: it is an indecency. And he recited:
فَكَيْفَ إِذَا رَأَيْتَ دِيَارَ قَوْمٍ * وَجِيرَانٍ لَنَا كَانُوا كِرَاْمِ
(How then, when you have seen the abodes of a people, and of neighbours of ours who were noble?)
Abū Jaʿfar said: Abū Isḥāq said: This in my view is a mistake, because if "كان" were redundant, it would have had to be "إنه كان فَاحِشَةٌ ومَقْتٌ" (in the nominative).
The [other] answer: that this was regarded as abominable among them in the Jāhiliyya; they called it an indecency and hateful (maqt).
Al-maqt is the most intense hatred, and they called the child born of it al-maqtī. So Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He, made known that this which He forbade was already ugly and hated in the Jāhiliyya.

nahhas-meani:23-23.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿حُرِّمَتْ عَلَيْكُمْ أُمَّهَاتُكُمْ وَبَنَاتُكُمْ وَأَخَوَاتُكُمْ وَعَمَّاتُكُمْ وَخَالاَتُكُمْ وَبَنَاتُ ٱلأَخِ وَبَنَاتُ ٱلأُخْتِ وَأُمَّهَاتُكُمُ اللاَّتِي أَرْضَعْنَكُمْ وَأَخَوَاتُكُم مِّنَ ٱلرَّضَاعَةِ وَأُمَّهَاتُ نِسَآئِكُمْ﴾.
These forbidden women are called al-mubhamāt (the unconditional ones), because they are not lawful in any way or for any reason — except His saying ﴿وَأُمَّهَاتُ نِسَآئِكُمْ﴾, for most of the jurists count it among the first [group].
Some of them said: If he married her and did not consummate the marriage with her, her mother is not forbidden to him.
This view is far-fetched according to the doctrine of the linguists, because the condition [applies] to whom it falls upon [Translator's note: so in the text, "لمن يقعْ عليه"; perhaps "لم يقع عليه" (it does not fall upon it) is intended], and because His saying ﴿مِّن نِّسَآئِكُمُ ٱللاَّتِي دَخَلْتُمْ بِهِنَّ﴾ is attached (mutaʿalliq) to His saying ﴿وَرَبَائِبُكُمُ ٱللاَّتِي فِي حُجُورِكُمْ﴾. It is not permissible for His saying (اللاتي) to be a naʿt (adjective) of both of them together, because the two governing expressions (khabarān) differ; but it is permissible in the sense of "I mean" (aʿnī).
Al-Khalīl and Sībawayh recited:
إنَّ بِهَا أَكْتَلَ أَوْرِزَامَا * خُوَيْرِبَيْنِ يَنْقُفَانِ الْهَامَا
(In it are Aktal and Rizām — two petty thieves who split open the skulls.)
"خُوَيْرِبَيْن" is in the sense of "I mean".
Al-rabība is: the daughter of a man's wife. She is called "rabība" because her mother's husband rears her (yurabbīhā). She may be called rabība even if he did not rear her, because she is of those whom he rears, just as one says uḍḥiya (sacrificial animal) before it has been sacrificed, and likewise ḥalūba, i.e. [an animal] that is milked. The poet said:
فيها اثْنَتَانِ وَأَرْبَعُونَ حَلُوبَةً * سُودَاً كَخَافِيَةِ الغُرابِ الأسْحَمِ
(Among them are forty-two milch camels, black like the hidden wing-feathers of the jet-black raven.)
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَحَلاَئِلُ أَبْنَائِكُمُ ٱلَّذِينَ مِنْ أَصْلاَبِكُمْ﴾.
A man's ḥalīla is his wife, and the man is ḥalīl, because each of them alights (yaḥillu) with the other.
It has also been said: ḥalīla is in the sense of muḥalla (made lawful), from lawful (ḥalāl) and unlawful. The poet said:
وَحَلِيلِ غَانِيَةٍ تَرَكْتُ مُجَدَّلاً * تَمْكُو فَرِيصَتُهُ كَشِدْقِ الأَعْلَمِ
(And many a husband of a beautiful woman have I left thrown to the ground, the muscle by his shoulder whistling [with blood] like the corner of a split-lipped man's mouth.)
As for the benefit of His saying ﴿مِنْ أَصْلاَبِكُمْ﴾, it is to exclude from this the wives of adopted sons; but (في حُجورِكُمْ) indicates rearing. [Translator's note: the text reads "الحليلات بنات الأدعياء" (the wives, the daughters of the adopted sons); "wives of the adopted sons" is evidently meant.]
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَأَن تَجْمَعُواْ بَيْنَ ٱلأُخْتَيْنِ إِلاَّ مَا قَدْ سَلَفَ﴾.
This is an exception not from the first [kind], and the meaning is: but what has already passed is forgiven.

nahhas-meani:24-24.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَٱلْمُحْصَنَاتُ مِنَ ٱلنِّسَآءِ﴾.
ʿAlī, Ibn ʿAbbās and Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī said: They are married women; none of them is lawful unless she is taken captive.
ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās said: Marrying married women is fornication, unless she is taken captive while having had a husband; then she becomes lawful by right of possession (milk al-yamīn).
Another view: that they are slave-women who have husbands; when ownership over them is newly established, it annuls their marriage.
This is related from Ibn Masʿūd, Ubayy ibn Kaʿb, Jābir and Anas.
A third view: Abū ʿUbayda said: ﴿إِلاَّ مَا مَلَكْتَ أَيْمَانُكُمْ﴾ means the four.
The best of them is the first, because of the ḥadīth of Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī: "We took captives on the day of Awṭās, and they had husbands, and we were reluctant to have intercourse with them. So we asked the Messenger of Allah, and this verse was revealed, and we took them as lawful."
* And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿كِتَابَ ٱللَّهِ عَلَيْكُمْ﴾.
That is: Allah's ordinance upon you.
It has also been read: ﴿كَتَبَ اللَّهُ عليكم﴾, i.e. Allah has ordained the prohibition of these.
He did not say that no others besides them are forbidden to you.
It is soundly established from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: "A woman is not to be married in addition to her paternal aunt, nor in addition to her maternal aunt."
And it is soundly established from him ﷺ that he said: "What is forbidden through lineage is forbidden through suckling."
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿أَن تَبْتَغُواْ بِأَمْوَالِكُمْ مُّحْصِنِينَ﴾.
﴿مُّحْصِنِينَ﴾, that is: marrying.
﴿غَيْرَ مُسَافِحِيْنَ﴾.
Mujāhid said: That is, not fornicating.
Its origin is from safaḥa, when one pours out, as the poet said:
وَإِنَّ شِفَائِي عَبْرَةٌ إنْ سَفَحْتُهَا * فَهَل عِنْدَ رَسْمٍِ دَارِسٍ مِنْ مُعَوَّلِ
(My cure is a tear, if I pour it out; but is there, at an effaced trace of an abode, anything to rely upon?)
So fornication was called "sifāḥ" because it is like poured-out water.
* And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿فَمَا اسْتَمْتَعْتُم بِهِ مِنْهُنَّ فَآتُوهَنَّ أُجُورَهُنَّ فَرِيضَةً﴾.
There are two views on the meaning of this verse:
One of them: that it is abrogated.
That is related from Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab.
ʿIkrima ibn ʿAmmār related from Saʿīd ibn Abī Saʿīd, from Abū Hurayra, from the Prophet ﷺ: "Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He, has forbidden — or annulled — the mutʿa (temporary marriage) by divorce, marriage, the waiting period (ʿidda) and inheritance."
Mālik related from al-Zuhrī that ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib — Allah's mercy be upon them — and al-Ḥasan ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī informed him that their father informed them that he heard ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, may Allah be pleased with him, say to Ibn ʿAbbās: "You are a man who has gone astray; the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade mutʿa."
ʿĀʾisha said: Allah forbade mutʿa by His saying: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ هُم لِفُرُوْجِهِمْ حَافِظُوْنَ. إِلاَّ عَلَى أَزْوَاجِهِمْ أَوْ مَا مَلَكَتْ أَيْمَانُهُمْ﴾.
The proof that "the woman taken in mutʿa" is not a wife is that if she were a wife, divorce would apply to her, she would have to observe the waiting period of widowhood, her child would be attributed to his father, and they would inherit from each other.
The meaning of ﴿فَآتُوهُنَّ أُجُورَهُنَّ﴾ is: the dower (mahr).
The proof of that is that after it comes ﴿فَٱنكِحُوهُنَّ بِإِذْنِ أَهْلِهِنَّ وَآتُوهُنَّ أُجُورَهُنَّ﴾.
And this, by consensus, is the dower.
It is related from Ubayy ibn Kaʿb and Ibn ʿAbbās that they read: ﴿فَمَا اسْتَمْتَعْتُمْ بِهِ مِنْهُنَّ إلَى أَجَلٍ مُسَمَّى﴾.
The other view: that this has nothing to do with mutʿa.
Al-Ḥasan and Mujāhid said: It concerns marriage.
So the meaning of ﴿فَمَا ٱسْتَمْتَعْتُمْ بِهِ مِنْهُنَّ﴾ is: through marriage.
That is: if you have consummated the marriage with her, she gets the dower; and whoever has not consummated owes half the dower.
The proof that this is the correct view is His saying: ﴿وَلاَ جُنَاحَ عَلَيْكُمْ فِيمَا تَرَاضَيْتُمْ بِهِ مِن بَعْدِ ٱلْفَرِيضَةِ﴾.
That is: if he gives her the other half [there is no blame], and if she gives him the half, there is no blame.
Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ كَانَ عَلِيماً حَكِيماً﴾.
That is: He is All-Knowing of what He has ordained for you in marriage.

nahhas-meani:25-25.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمَن لَّمْ يَسْتَطِعْ مِنكُمْ طَوْلاً﴾.
That is: the means to pay the dower.
Al-ṭawl in the language is: surplus (bounty); and from it: "Allah taṭawwala (bestowed His bounty) upon us".
Al-ṭūl in stature is a surplus; al-ṭiwal is: the rope; and one says: "I will speak to him for ṭawāl (the whole length) of time."
There are two views on His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He, ﴿أَن يَنكِحَ ٱلْمُحْصَنَاتِ﴾:
One of them: that they are the chaste women.
And the other: that they are the free women.
The more likely is that they are the free women, [because of His saying]: ﴿فَمِنْ مَّا مَلَكَتْ أَيْمَانُكُم مِّن فَتَيَاتِكُمُ ٱلْمُؤْمِنَاتِ﴾, meaning the slave-women.
The Arabs call a male slave fatā and a female slave fatāt.
Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿بَعْضُكُمْ مِّن بَعْضٍ﴾.
There are two views on the meaning of this:
One of them: [you are all] the children of Adam.
And the other view: you are believers, so you are brothers.
This was said to them, according to what is related, only because in the Jāhiliyya they used to taunt one another with mixed descent (hujna), and called the son of a slave-woman hajīn; so He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿بَعْضُكُم مِّن بَعْضٍ﴾.
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَآتُوهُنَّ أُجُورَهُنَّ بِٱلْمَعْرُوفِ مُحْصَنَاتٍ﴾, i.e. married, ﴿غَيْرَ مُسَافِحَاتٍ﴾.
That is: not fornicating; ﴿وَلاَ مُتَّخِذَاتِ أَخْدَانٍ﴾.
Al-khidn is: the [secret] friend; i.e. not fornicating with one [lover] nor freely available [to all].
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty is He, said: ﴿فَإِذَآ أُحْصِنَّ﴾.
Al-Shaʿbī said: Its meaning is: and when they have accepted Islam.
It is related from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd that he said: al-iḥṣān is: Islam.
It is also read "فإذا أُحْصِنَّ" [Translator's note: the two readings are not distinguished by vowelling in the text; the reading meant is evidently "أَحْصَنَّ" with fatḥa versus "أُحْصِنَّ" with ḍamma].
Ibn ʿAbbās said: [It means] they are given in marriage, if she was unmarried.
Al-Zuhrī said: Its meaning is: and when they are married. Al-Zuhrī said: The slave-woman receives the ḥadd if she fornicates while married, by the Book; and she receives the ḥadd if she fornicates while not married, by the Sunna.
The preferred [reading] among the people of reasoned investigation is "فَإِذَا أُحْصِنَّ" with ḍamma, because their being Muslim has already been mentioned in His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمَن لَّمْ يَسْتَطِعْ مِنكُمْ طَوْلاً أَن يَنكِحَ ٱلْمُحْصَنَاتِ ٱلْمُؤْمِنَاتِ﴾.
That shows that the second iḥṣān is something other than Islam; so on this basis the preferred [reading] is ﴿أُحْصِنَّ﴾ with ḍamma, i.e. they have been married.
It has also been said: ﴿أَحْصَنَّ﴾ means they married; and this is more fitting, because He said ﴿مِّن فَتَيَاتِكُمُ ٱلْمُؤْمِنَاتِ﴾, so it is unlikely that He would say: and when they have accepted Islam.
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty is He, said: ﴿فَعَلَيْهِنَّ نِصْفُ مَا عَلَى ٱلْمُحْصَنَاتِ مِنَ ٱلْعَذَابِ﴾.
He means half the ḥadd; and by al-muḥṣanāt here He means free virgins, because the previously married woman is liable to stoning, which cannot be divided.
It has been said: the virgin is called muḥṣana, even though she is not married, only because iḥṣān will be hers, just as one says uḍḥiya before it has been sacrificed, and as one calls the cow muthīra (ploughing) before it ploughs.
It has also been said: «المحصَنَاتُ» are the married women, because they are liable to beating and stoning according to the ḥadīth, and stoning cannot be divided, so they [the slave-women] became liable to half the beating.
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty is He, said: ﴿ذَلِكَ لِمَنْ خَشِيَ ٱلْعَنَتَ مِنْكُمْ﴾.
Al-Shaʿbī said: He means fornication.
Al-ʿanat in the language is: hardship. One says: "an ʿanūt hill", when it is hard [to climb].
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty is He, said: ﴿وَأَن تَصْبِرُواْ خَيْرٌ لَّكُمْ﴾.
That is: and that you be patient in refraining from marrying slave-women is better for you. He was strict regarding slave-women only because a man's child by her is a slave, and she is put to menial service, and this is hard on the husband.

nahhas-meani:26-26.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَيَهْدِيَكُمْ سُنَنَ ٱلَّذِينَ مِن قَبْلِكُمْ﴾.
That is: the ways of the prophets and the righteous before you, so that you may follow them.

nahhas-meani:27-27.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَيُرِيدُ ٱلَّذِينَ يَتَّبِعُونَ ٱلشَّهَوَاتِ أَن تَمِيلُواْ مَيْلاً عَظِيماً﴾.
That is: they want you to turn aside from the right course and the truth.

nahhas-meani:28-28.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿يُرِيدُ ٱللَّهُ أَن يُخَفِّفَ عَنْكُمْ وَخُلِقَ ٱلإِنسَانُ ضَعِيفاً﴾.
Ṭāwūs said: He was created weak with regard to the matter of women in particular.
It is related from Ibn ʿAbbās that he read: ﴿وَخَلَقَ الإِنَسَانَ ضَعِيفَاً﴾, i.e. Allah created man weak.

nahhas-meani:29-29.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ لاَ تَأْكُلُوۤاْ أَمْوَالَكُمْ بَيْنَكُمْ بِٱلْبَاطِلِ﴾.
That is: it is not lawful for you except in accordance with what has been set out before: a gift, a dower, a charity, a sale, a purchase and the like [Translator's note: the text reads "وما أشبه لك", evidently for "وما أشبه ذلك"].
* And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَلاَ تَقْتُلُوۤاْ أَنْفُسَكُمْ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ كَانَ بِكُمْ رَحِيماً﴾.
ʿAṭāʾ said: That is, let not some of you kill others.
That is well known in the language, because the believer is to the believer like his own self.
Al-Ḥasan read: ﴿وَلاَ تَقْتُلُوۤاْ أَنْفُسَكُمْ﴾ in the intensive form [Translator's note: the word is printed here as in the standard reading; the intensive form meant is presumably "تُقَتِّلُوا"].

nahhas-meani:30-30.t:
Then He, Majestic and Mighty is He, said: ﴿وَمَن يَفْعَلْ ذٰلِكَ عُدْوَاناً وَظُلْماً فَسَوْفَ نُصْلِيهِ نَاراً﴾.
Al-ʿudwān in the language is: transgressing beyond what is right.
And al-ẓulm is: putting a thing in other than its proper place.
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty is He, said: ﴿وَكَانَ ذٰلِكَ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ يَسِيراً﴾.
That is: easy. One says: yasura the thing, so it is yasīr, when it became easy.

nahhas-meani:31-31.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿إِن تَجْتَنِبُواْ كَبَآئِرَ مَا تُنْهَوْنَ عَنْهُ﴾.
ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, may Allah be pleased with him, said: The major sins are: associating partners with Allah, sorcery, slandering a chaste woman, consuming usury, consuming the wealth of the orphan, fleeing from the battle line, and undutifulness to parents.
ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd said: The major sins are: associating partners with Allah, despairing of the mercy of Allah, losing hope of the relief of (Allah), and feeling secure from the plan of Allah.
Ṭāwūs said: It was said to Ibn ʿAbbās: Are the major sins seven?
He said: They are nearer to seventy.
The real sense of "major sin" (kabīra) in the language is: that which is great and grave, for which Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He, has threatened the Fire, or in which He has ordered a punishment; what is other than these two may be either a major or a minor sin.
* Then He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿نُكَفِّرْ عَنْكُمْ سَيِّئَآتِكُم﴾.
Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī said, from the Prophet ﷺ: "No Muslim is afflicted by worry or fatigue but that [some of his sins] are expiated for him by it."
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty is He, said: ﴿وَنُدْخِلْكُمْ مُّدْخَلاً كَرِيماً﴾.
It has been said: He means by it Paradise, and Allah knows best.

nahhas-meani:32-32.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَلاَ تَتَمَنَّوْاْ مَا فَضَّلَ ٱللَّهُ بِهِ بَعْضَكُمْ عَلَىٰ بَعْضٍ﴾.
It is related that Umm Salama said: O Messenger of Allah, Allah has favoured men over women with fighting and in inheritance. So Allah revealed: ﴿وَلاَ تَتَمَنَّوْاْ مَا فَضَّلَ ٱللَّهُ بِهِ بَعْضَكُمْ عَلَىٰ بَعْضٍ﴾.
It has also been said: Only envy (ḥasad) was forbidden.
Envy according to the linguists is that a person wishes for what another has, in that it should cease from him; if he wishes for what another has without wanting it to cease from him, that is called ghibṭa (emulation).
The meaning [on this view]: and do not wish for the "loss" of what…; then [the muḍāf] was omitted.
Qatāda said: The "people" of the Jāhiliyya used not to let women or children inherit. When they were made heirs, and the male was given the like of the share of two females, the women wished that their shares had been made like the shares of the men; and the men said: We hope to be favoured over the women by our good deeds in the Hereafter, just as we have been favoured over them in inheritance. So there was revealed: ﴿وَلاَ تَتَمَنَّوْاْ مَا فَضَّلَ ٱللَّهُ بِهِ بَعْضَكُمْ عَلَىٰ بَعْضٍ، لِّلرِّجَالِ نَصِيبٌ مِّمَّا ٱكْتَسَبُواْ وَلِلنِّسَآءِ نَصِيبٌ مِّمَّا ٱكْتَسَبْنَ﴾, i.e. a woman is rewarded for her good deed ten times its like, just as men are rewarded.
Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said: ﴿وَٱسْأَلُواْ ٱللَّهَ مِن فَضْلِهِ﴾ —
[it means] worship; it is not about the affairs of this world.
It has also been said: Ask Him for success in doing what pleases Him.
﴿إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ كَانَ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ عَلِيماً﴾, that is: [knowing] of what sets His servants right.

nahhas-meani:33-33.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَلِكُلٍّ جَعَلْنَا مَوَالِيَ مِمَّا تَرَكَ ٱلْوَالِدَانِ وَٱلأَقْرَبُونَ﴾.
Mujāhid said: They are the paternal cousins.
Qatāda said: They are the relatives, among them the father and the brother.
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: He means the relatives.
And this is the view of most of the linguists.
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَٱلَّذِينَ عَقَدَتْ أَيْمَانُكُمْ فَآتُوهُمْ نَصِيبَهُمْ﴾.
This verse is abrogated.
Ibn ʿAbbās said: In the Jāhiliyya a man would come to another man and say to him: I will inherit from you and you will inherit from me; and that would be a pact of alliance between them. Then Allah abrogated that by His saying: ﴿وَأُولُوا الأَرْحامِ، بَعْضُهُمْ أَوْلَى بِبَعْضٍ فِيْ كِتَاْبِ اللَّهِ﴾.
Likewise it is related from al-Ḥasan, ʿIkrima and Qatāda that the verse is abrogated.
Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab said: A man would adopt a man, and they would inherit from each other on that basis; [then] Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He, [abrogated it].

nahhas-meani:34-34.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿ٱلرِّجَالُ قَوَّامُونَ عَلَى ٱلنِّسَآءِ﴾.
It has been said: Because among them are the judges, the commanders and those who go out to fight.
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty is He, said: ﴿بِمَا فَضَّلَ ٱللَّهُ بَعْضَهُمْ عَلَىٰ بَعْضٍ وَبِمَآ أَنْفَقُواْ مِنْ أَمْوَالِهِمْ﴾.
That is: of the dowers.
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty is He, said: ﴿فَٱلصَّالِحَاتُ قَانِتَاتٌ﴾.
Qatāda said: That is, obedient.
Someone else said: That is, attending to their husbands' affairs as is required by their due.
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty is He, said: ﴿حَافِظَاتٌ لِّلْغَيْبِ﴾.
Qatāda said: That is, in their husbands' absence.
﴿بِمَا حَفِظَ ٱللَّهُ﴾, that is: by what Allah has safeguarded them with, in their dowers and in spending on them.
Abū Jaʿfar al-Madanī read: ﴿بِمَا حَفِظَ اللَّهَ﴾.
Its meaning is: by their having kept [the rights of] Allah in obedience; its implied construction is: by keeping [the rights of] Allah.
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَٱللاَّتِي تَخَافُونَ نُشُوزَهُنَّ فَعِظُوهُنَّ﴾.
The exegetes said: al-nushūz is: hostility.
Al-nushūz in the language is: rising up; and raised ground is called nashz and nashaz.
And hostility is: rising above what is required, and departing from it.
Sufyān said: the meaning of ﴿فَعِظُوْهُنَّ﴾ is: admonish them by [reminding them of] Allah.
﴿وَٱهْجُرُوهُنَّ فِي ٱلْمَضَاجِعِ﴾.
Sufyān said: Without abandoning intercourse.
﴿وَٱضْرِبُوهُنَّ﴾.
ʿAṭāʾ said: A beating that is not severe.
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty is He, said: ﴿فَإِنْ أَطَعْنَكُمْ فَلاَ تَبْغُواْ عَلَيْهِنَّ سَبِيلاً﴾.
Ibn Juraykh [Translator's note: so in the text, "ابن جريح"; presumably Ibn Jurayj] said: That is, do not seek a way of causing them hardship.
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty is He, said: ﴿إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ كَانَ عَلِيّاً كَبِيراً﴾.
That is: He is exalted above imposing anything but what is right and within the measure of one's capacity.

nahhas-meani:35-35.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَإِنْ خِفْتُمْ شِقَاقَ بَيْنِهِمَا﴾.
Abū ʿUbayda said: The meaning of ﴿خِفْتُمْ﴾ is: you are certain.
Abū Jaʿfar said: Abū Isḥāq said: This in my view is a mistake, because if we were certain, there would be no need for the two arbiters; "خِفْتُمْ" here is in its proper sense (ʿalā bābihā).
Al-shiqāq is: hostility; its real sense is that each of the two who are hostile is on a side (shiqq) other than his companion's side.
Mujāhid said: He means the two arbiters. [Translator's note: this evidently refers to the phrase ﴿إِن يُرِيدَآ إِصْلاَحاً﴾ later in the verse, which is not quoted here.]
Abū Jaʿfar said: This is a good view, because if the two of them agree, it is accepted from them — though there is disagreement about that.
It is related from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr that he said: The two arbiters may pronounce divorce on the man's behalf if they agree on that; and this is the view of Mālik.
There is another view on it: that they do not pronounce divorce on his behalf until he consents to their ruling.
Ayyūb and Hishām related this view from Muḥammad ibn Sīrīn, from ʿAbīda, from ʿAlī — may Allah have mercy on him — that he said to the two arbiters: "You may bring them together and you may separate them." The husband said: As for separation, no. ʿAlī said: By Allah, you shall consent to the Book of Allah!
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty is He, said: ﴿إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ كَانَ عَلِيماً خَبِيراً﴾.
That is: He is All-Knowing of what contains well-being, All-Aware of that.

nahhas-meani:127-127.t:
His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَيَسْتَفْتُونَكَ فِي ٱلنِّسَآءِ قُلِ ٱللَّهُ يُفْتِيكُمْ فِيهِنَّ وَمَا يُتْلَىٰ عَلَيْكُمْ فِي ٱلْكِتَابِ﴾.
(مَا) is in the position of the nominative; the meaning is: say: Allah gives you a ruling concerning them, and the Qurʾān gives you a ruling concerning them.
That which gives you a ruling from the Qurʾān concerning women is His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَانْكِحُوا مَا طَابَ لَكُمْ مِنَ النِّسَاءِ مَثْنَى وَثُلاَثَ وَرُبَاعَ﴾.
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿فِي يَتَامَى ٱلنِّسَآءِ ٱلَّلاتِي لاَ تُؤْتُونَهُنَّ مَا كُتِبَ لَهُنَّ وَتَرْغَبُونَ أَن تَنكِحُوهُنَّ﴾.
ʿĀʾisha, may Allah have mercy on her, said: this concerns the orphan girl who is in a man's care. ﴿وَتَرْغَبُونَ أَن تَنكِحُوهُنَّ﴾: the aversion of one of you to his orphan girl who is in his guardianship, when she has little wealth and beauty; so they were forbidden to marry those orphan girls whose wealth and beauty they desired, except with equity.
In some narrations from her: this concerns the orphan girl who may be his partner in wealth, and he does not want to marry her, nor does he like her to marry someone else, lest that man take her wealth. Allah, exalted be His name, said: ﴿وَتَرْغَبُونَ أَن تَنكِحُوْهُنَّ﴾.
Saʿīd ibn Jubayr and Mujāhid said: and he desires to marry her when she has much wealth.
The linguists have two implied constructions for this:
One of them: that the meaning is «and you are averse [عن] to marrying them» (ترغبون عن), then عن was omitted.
The ḥadīth of ʿĀʾisha strengthens this view.
The other view: «and you desire (ترغبون في) to marry them», then «في» was omitted.
If you reflect on the statement of "Saʿīd ibn Jubayr", you will see that he has brought both meanings.
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿وَٱلْمُسْتَضْعَفِينَ مِنَ ٱلْوِلْدَانِ﴾.
Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said: they used not to let the young inherit, so there was revealed: ﴿يُوْصِيكُمُ اللَّهُ فِي أَوْلاَدِكُمْ لِلذَّكَرِ مِثْلُ حَظِّ الأُنْثَيينِ﴾.
So according to the view of Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, what gave them a ruling regarding the oppressed is His saying: ﴿يُوْصِيكُمُ اللَّهُ فِي أَوْلاَدِكُمْ﴾.
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿وَأَن تَقُومُواْ لِلْيَتَامَىٰ بِٱلْقِسْطِ﴾.
القسط is justice; and what gave them a ruling regarding orphans is His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَلاَ تَأكُلُوْا أَمَوْالَهُمْ إِلَى أَمْوَالِكُمْ﴾.

nahhas-meani:128-128.t:
His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَإِنِ ٱمْرَأَةٌ خَافَتْ مِن بَعْلِهَا نُشُوزاً أَوْ إِعْرَاضاً﴾.
[النشوز on the husband's part is that he treats her badly and withholds from her his company and his maintenance.]
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿فَلاَ جُنَاْحَ عَلَيْهِمَآ أَن يَصَّالَحَا بَيْنَهُمَا صُلْحاً﴾.
Most of the Kufans read: ﴿أَنْ يُصْلِحَا﴾.
Al-Jaḥdarī and ʿUthmān al-Battī read: ﴿أَنْ يَصَّلِحَا﴾.
The meaning is يصطلحا, then it was assimilated.
As for the exegesis of the verse, Simāk ibn Ḥarb narrated from Khālid ibn ʿArʿara, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: "She is the woman who is with a man, and she is unattractive or old, and she dislikes separating from him; so they come to terms that he visits her every three or four days."
ʿĀʾisha said: it is the man who has a wife; perhaps he has no child by her [and does not love her], so he wants to let her go; so she comes to terms with him and says: do not divorce me, and you are free of obligation regarding my affairs.
Al-Zuhrī narrated from Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab and Sulaymān ibn Yasār that this verse was revealed concerning "Rāfiʿ ibn Khadīj": he divorced his wife once and married a young woman. When the end of the waiting period drew near, she said to him: I will come to terms with you over some of the days. So he took her back; then she could not bear it, so he divorced her again; then she asked him for that, and he took her back; and this verse was revealed.
In the ḥadīth of Hishām ibn ʿUrwa, from his father, from ʿĀʾisha: Sawda gave her day to ʿĀʾisha, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would allot to ʿĀʾisha her own day and Sawda's day; by that Sawda sought the pleasure of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿وَٱلصُّلْحُ خَيْرٌ﴾.
The meaning is: reconciliation is better than separation; then this was omitted because the hearer knows it.
And it is said, regarding the meaning of «الله أكبر»: Allah is greater than everything.
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿وَأُحْضِرَتِ ٱلأنْفُسُ ٱلشُّحَّ﴾.
ʿAṭāʾ said: He means stinginess regarding the days and the maintenance.
The meaning of this is that the woman is stingy about the maintenance spent on her co-wives and his preferring them.
Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said: this concerns the woman who is stingy with wealth and with herself.

nahhas-meani:129-129.t:
His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَلَن تَسْتَطِيعُوۤاْ أَن تَعْدِلُواْ بَيْنَ ٱلنِّسَآءِ وَلَوْ حَرَصْتُمْ﴾.
ʿAbīda said: in love and intercourse.
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿فَلاَ تَمِيلُواْ كُلَّ ٱلْمَيْلِ﴾.
ʿAbīda said: he means with your selves.
Mujāhid said: do not deliberately do harm.
The meaning is: divide between them equally.
It is narrated from ʿĀʾisha, may Allah have mercy on her, that she said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to divide between his wives with justice, then say: O Allah, this is what I control, so do not hold me to account for what You control and I do not control."
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿فَتَذَرُوهَا كَٱلْمُعَلَّقَةِ﴾.
Al-Ḥasan said: she is the one who has no husband [for her] and is not divorced either.
Qatāda said: like the one confined and like the one imprisoned.

nahhas-meani:134-134.t:
His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿مَّن كَانَ يُرِيدُ ثَوَابَ ٱلدُّنْيَا فَعِندَ ٱللَّهِ ثَوَابُ ٱلدُّنْيَا وَٱلآخِرَةِ﴾.
It is narrated that most of the polytheists did not believe in the Resurrection, and sought nearness to Allah only so that He would grant them plenty in this world and ward off its hardships from them; so Allah revealed: ﴿مَّن كَانَ يُرِيدُ ثَوَابَ ٱلدُّنْيَا فَعِندَ ٱللَّهِ ثَوَابُ ٱلدُّنْيَا وَٱلآخِرَةِ﴾.

nahhas-meani:135-135.t:
His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ كُونُواْ قَوَّامِينَ بِٱلْقِسْطِ﴾.
القِسط and الإقساط are justice. One says أَقْسَطَ يُقْسِطُ إقساطاً when he acts justly, and قَسَطَ يَقْسِطُ when he acts unjustly.
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿شُهَدَآءِ للَّهِ وَلَوْ عَلَىۤ أَنْفُسِكُمْ أَوِ ٱلْوَالِدَيْنِ وَٱلأَقْرَبِينَ إِن يَكُنْ غَنِيّاً أَوْ فَقِيراً فَٱللَّهُ أَوْلَىٰ بِهِمَا﴾.
The meaning is: if the one in whose favour testimony is given is rich, let that not prevent you from testifying; and if the one against whom testimony is given is poor, let that not prevent you from testifying against him.
If it is asked: how does one uphold testimony against himself? Does one testify against himself?
It is answered: he owes a right to someone else and acknowledges it to him; that is his upholding of testimony against himself.
Allah, Mighty and Majestic, disciplined the believers [by this], as Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah have mercy on him, said: they were commanded to speak the truth even against themselves.
Then He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿فَلاَ تَتَّبِعُواْ ٱلْهَوَىٰ أَن تَعْدِلُواْ﴾.
The meaning is: do not follow desire, so that you may act justly; and render the testimony you have.
This is the view of most of the linguists.
It is possible that the meaning is: do not follow desire out of aversion to acting justly, because when one opposes the truth it is as though he disliked justice.
* Then He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿وَإِن تَلْوُواْ أَوْ تُعْرِضُواْ﴾.
Qābūs ibn Abī Ẓibyān narrated from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: "It concerns two litigants who come before the judge, and his twisting is in favour of one of them and his turning away is from the other."
Mujāhid said: ﴿وَإِن تَلْوُواْ﴾, that is, you alter, ﴿أَو تُعْرِضوُا﴾, you abandon.
So the position of Ibn ʿAbbās is that the twisting is by the judge, and the position of Mujāhid is that it is by the witness.
Likewise al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: it is that he twists his tongue away from the truth in testimony, or turns away and conceals it.
The root of لوى in the language is: to put off (a debt).
Sībawayh recited:
قَدْ كُنْتُ دَايَنْتُ بها حَسَّانَا * مَخَافَةَ الإِفلاَسِ والَّليَانَيا
(I had sold her on credit to Ḥassān, fearing bankruptcy and delay in payment.)
It has also been read: ﴿وَإِنْ تَلُوْا أَوْ تُعْرِضُوْا﴾. There are two views on it:
One of them is al-Kisāʾī's; he said: the meaning is from الولاية (taking charge): if you take charge of something or leave it.
Abū Isḥāq said: whoever reads (وَإِنْ تَلُوْا), the meaning according to his reading is وإن تَلْوُوا; then he made the first واو a hamza, so it became تَلْؤُوا — as he said: one says أَدْؤُر in the plural of دار — then he cast the vowel of the hamza onto the lām and dropped the hamza, so it became تَلُوا, just as one says آدُر in the plural of دار.

nahhas-meani:136-136.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ آمِنُواْ بِٱللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ﴾.
There are two views on its meaning:
One of them: remain firm in faith, just as one says to someone standing: stand until I come,
that is, remain standing.
The other view: that it is addressed to the hypocrites; the meaning on this view is: O you who believe outwardly, be sincere to Allah.

nahhas-meani:137-137.t:
His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ ثُمَّ كَفَرُواْ ثُمَّ آمَنُواْ ثُمَّ كَفَرُواْ ثُمَّ ٱزْدَادُواْ كُفْراً لَّمْ يَكُنِ ٱللَّهُ لِيَغْفِرَ لَهُمْ وَلاَ لِيَهْدِيَهُمْ سَبِيلاً﴾ — [verse 137].
Mujāhid said: the hypocrites are meant by it.
He said: and the meaning of ﴿ثُمَّ ٱزْدَادُواْ كُفْراً﴾ is:
they died in that state.
This view is not far-fetched linguistically, because when they died in disbelief they perished, so they are in the position of one who increased in disbelief.
Abū al-ʿĀliya said: ﴿إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ ثُمَّ كَفَرُواْ﴾: the Jews and the Christians disbelieved; ﴿ثُمَّ ٱزْدَادُواْ كُفْراً﴾: through sins they committed. «[Translator's note: the source writes «أبو عالية» for Abū al-ʿĀliya.]»
Qatāda said: ﴿ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ ثُمَّ كَفَرُواْ﴾ are the Jews and the Christians. The Jews believed in the Torah, then disbelieved — meaning in the Gospel; then they believed in ʿUzayr, then disbelieved in ʿĪsā; then they increased in disbelief by their disbelief in Muḥammad ﷺ.
And the Christians believed in the Gospel, then disbelieved, their disbelief in it being their abandoning it; then they increased in disbelief through the Qurʾān and Muḥammad, upon him be peace.

nahhas-meani:138-138.t:
His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿بَشِّرِ ٱلْمُنَافِقِينَ بِأَنَّ لَهُمْ عَذَاباً أَلِيماً﴾.
[The meaning:] make the punishment that which stands for them in place of good tidings.
Sībawayh recited:
وَخَيْلٍ قَدْ دَلَفْتُ لَهَا بِخَيْلٍ * تَحِيَّةُ بَيْنِهِمْ ضَرْبٌ وَجِيعُ
(Many a troop of horse have I advanced against with horse; the greeting between them is a painful blow.)
That is: what stands in place of the greeting is a painful blow.

nahhas-meani:139-139.t:
His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿أَيَبْتَغُونَ عِندَهُمُ ٱلْعِزَّةَ﴾? [verse 139].
Do the hypocrites seek العزة with the unbelievers? That is, protective strength.
Al-Aṣmaʿī said: one says «أرض عَزاز», with fatḥa and kasra, when the ground is hard and firm; and their saying «يعزّ عليّ», that is, it is hard upon me.
From it is His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿وَعَزَّنِي فِي الْخِطَابِ﴾, that is, he overpowered me because he is stronger than me.
From it is their saying: "مَن عَزَّ بَزَّ", that is, whoever prevails takes the spoils.
From it is the saying: "فعزّته يداه وكاهله" (his two hands and his shoulders overpowered him).

nahhas-meani:141-141.t:
His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿قَالُوۤاْ أَلَمْ نَسْتَحْوِذْ عَلَيْكُمْ﴾.
One says استحوذ [عليه] when he has gained mastery over him.
So the meaning is: the hypocrites said to the unbelievers: did we not prevail over you by our allegiance to you, and protect you from the believers? That is, we informed you of their news so that you might beware of what would come from them.
His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَلَن يَجْعَلَ ٱللَّهُ لِلْكَافِرِينَ عَلَى ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ سَبِيلاً﴾.
It is narrated from ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: that is in the Hereafter.
Ibn ʿAbbās said: that is the Day of Resurrection.
Al-Suddī said: السبيل is the argument.
And it is said: the meaning is that Allah helps the believers with argument and with victory, so as to make their religion prevail over all religion.

nahhas-meani:142-142.t:
His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿إِنَّ ٱلْمُنَافِقِينَ يُخَادِعُونَ ٱللَّهَ وَهُوَ خَادِعُهُمْ﴾.
The linguists said: the second is called deception because it is a requital for the first, so it is called deception by way of pairing (al-izdiwāj), as He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿وَجَزَاءُ سَيِّئَةٍ سَيِّئَةٌ مِثْلُهَا﴾.
Al-Ḥasan said: on the Day of Resurrection the believers and the hypocrites will be given a light; when they reach the Path (al-Ṣirāṭ), the light of the hypocrites will be extinguished, and the believers will become anxious and say: "Our Lord, perfect for us our light." So the believers will go on with their light, and they will call out to them: ﴿انْظُرُونَا نَقْتَبِس مِن نُورِكُم﴾, the verse.
Al-Ḥasan said: that is Allah's deception of them.
This view does not depart from the view of the linguists, because He called it deception since it is a requital for them.
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿وَإِذَا قَامُوۤاْ إِلَى ٱلصَّلاَةِ قَامُواْ كُسَالَىٰ يُرَآءُونَ ٱلنَّاسَ وَلاَ يَذْكُرُونَ ٱللَّهَ إِلاَّ قَلِيلاً﴾.
Al-Ḥasan said: it is little only because it is for other than Allah.
It is narrated from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: "No deed is little when accompanied by piety; how can that which is accepted be little?!"

nahhas-meani:143-143.t:
Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿مُّذَبْذَبِينَ بَيْنَ ذٰلِكَ لاَ إِلَىٰ هَـٰؤُلاۤءِ وَلاَ إِلَى هَـٰؤُلاۤءِ﴾.
Qatāda said: they are neither sincere in faith nor open in disbelief.
ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿUmar narrated from Nāfiʿ, from Ibn ʿUmar, that the Prophet ﷺ said: "The likeness of the hypocrite is that of the ewe straying between two flocks: when she comes to this one, it butts her, and when she comes to that one, it butts her; so she follows neither this one nor that one." «[Translator's note: the source has «فلا نتبع» (so we follow), evidently for «فلا تتبع» (so she follows); translated per the evident sense.]»
The root of التذبذب in the language is moving and wavering, as he said:
أَلَمْ تَرَ أَنَّ اللَّهَ أَعْطَاكَ سُوْرَةً * تَرَى كُلَّ مَلْكِ دُوْنَهَا يَتَذَبْذَبُ
(Do you not see that Allah has given you a rank of eminence, beneath which you see every king wavering?)
So the meaning is: the hypocrites are bewildered in their religion; they do not settle on believing anything soundly; they are neither with the believers in clear insight nor with the polytheists in ignorance, so they are bewildered between that.
النفاق (hypocrisy) is taken from النافقاء, which is one of the holes of the jerboa: when the exits are blocked against it, it comes out of it without being noticed.
Likewise the hypocrite outwardly shows Islam and secretly goes out of it.
In the ḥadīth: "The hypocrite has three signs: when he speaks he lies, when he promises he breaks it, and when he is entrusted he betrays."

nahhas-meani:144-144.t:
His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿أَتُرِيدُونَ أَن تَجْعَلُواْ للَّهِ عَلَيْكُمْ سُلْطَاناً مُّبِيناً﴾?
Qatāda said: السلطان is the argument.
And so it is according to the linguists.

nahhas-meani:145-145.t:
His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿إِنَّ ٱلْمُنَافِقِينَ فِي ٱلدَّرْكِ ٱلأَسْفَلِ مِنَ ٱلنَّارِ﴾.
ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd said: "They will be put in coffins of iron that are locked upon them"; and in some of the ḥadīth: of fire, then they are closed over them.
الأدراك in the language are the stations and the levels.

nahhas-meani:147-148.t:
His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿مَّا يَفْعَلُ ٱللَّهُ بِعَذَابِكُمْ إِن شَكَرْتُمْ وَآمَنْتُمْ وَكَانَ ٱللَّهُ شَاكِراً عَلِيماً. لاَّ يُحِبُّ ٱللَّهُ ٱلْجَهْرَ بِٱلسُّوۤءِ مِنَ ٱلْقَوْلِ إِلاَّ مَن ظُلِمَ﴾ [verses 147 - 148].
Zayd ibn Aslam and Ibn Abī Isḥāq read: ﴿إِلاَّ مَنْ ظَلَمَ﴾.
On this reading there are three views:
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: the meaning is: what would Allah do with punishing you — except the one who does wrong.
And it is said: the meaning is: let no one speak evil openly, except the one who does wrong, for he speaks it openly out of transgression.
Abū Isḥāq al-Zajjāj said: it is possible that the meaning is: except one who does wrong and says something evil, for you ought to restrain him; and it is an exception not of the same kind as what precedes.
On the first two answers it is also an exception not of the same kind as what precedes.
Whoever reads ﴿إِلاَّ مَنْ ظُلِمَ﴾, there are several views on it:
One of them: it is narrated from Mujāhid that he said: "This verse was revealed concerning a man who was a guest of some people and they did not treat him well; he mentioned what they had done, and they reproached him for it; so there was revealed: ﴿لاَّ يُحِبُّ ٱللَّهُ ٱلْجَهْرَ بِٱلسُّوۤءِ مِنَ ٱلْقَوْلِ إِلاَّ مَن ظُلِمَ﴾."
So the meaning on this view is: but whoever has been wronged may mention what was done to him.
Al-Ḥasan said: "This concerns the man who is wronged: he should not invoke evil upon the one who wronged him, but let him say: O Allah, help me against him, and extract my right from him, and the like."
Quṭrub said: ﴿إِلاَّ مَن ظُلِمَ﴾ — He means only the one under compulsion, because he is wronged, and that is lifted from him even if he utters disbelief.
He said: and it is possible that the meaning of ﴿إِلاَّ مَن ظُلِمَ﴾ is by way of badal (substitute), as though: Allah does not love except the one who is wronged, that is, He does not love the wrongdoer; it is as though He says: He loves the one who is wronged, that is, He rewards the one who is wronged.
The implied construction on this view is: «Allah does not love one who speaks evil openly, except the one who is wronged», by way of badal.
